sections.label: WP support for Budget 2024
sections.summary: The Workers' Party supports Budget 2024 because it is not objectionable in fleshing out the Government's direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In the way it fleshes out the direction of the Government, Budget 2024 is not objectionable, and so the Workers' Party (WP) supports the Budget.

sections.label: WP proposals in Budget
sections.summary: This year's Budget includes WP proposals, such as the Finance Minister's temporary financial support scheme for workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Indeed, this year's Budget includes WP proposals; the announcement by the Finance Minister of a temporary financial support scheme for our workers is a case in point.

sections.label: Budget marksmanship tax variations
sections.summary: The author noted Budget marksmanship would become more difficult as specific tax collections could vary 17% to 27%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The author noted that it would become more difficult to achieve Budget marksmanship as there could be variations of 17% to 27% in specific tax collections.

sections.label: 2016 industry transformation roadmap
sections.summary: In 2016, the Government announced a $4.5 billion industry transformation roadmap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Similarly, in 2016, the Government announced a $4.5 billion industry transformation roadmap.

sections.label: Forward Singapore budget financing
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister announced $5 billion of this Budget for Forward Singapore policy moves, with around $40 billion used by the decade's end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Coming back to the financing of Forward Singapore's goals, the Deputy Prime Minister announced that $5 billion of this Budget has been set aside for Forward Singapore policy moves, with around $40 billion to be used by the end of the decade.

sections.label: Singaporeans' affordability and retirement
sections.summary: 40% of Singaporeans can afford to spend beyond basics, down 8% from 2022; 23% can only afford basics; 79% lack or are off-track on retirement plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Just 40% of Singaporeans can afford to spend beyond the basics most of the time, down 8% from 2022; and 23% can only afford the basics; while 79% of Singaporeans either do not have a retirement plan or are not on track with their retirement plans.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credit for courses
sections.summary: The $4,000 SkillsFuture credit is ringfenced for selected programmes with better employability outcomes and can be used for part-time diploma, post-diploma, undergraduate and PWM-specific courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The $4,000 SkillsFuture credit, which is ringfenced for selected programmes with better employability outcomes, can be used for part-time diploma, post-diploma and undergraduate courses as well as PWM-specific courses.

sections.label: CPF top-ups for Singaporeans
sections.summary: In total, 1.4 million Singaporeans will see CPF top-ups.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In total, 1.4 million Singaporeans will see CPF top-ups.

sections.label: CPF use for HDB flats
sections.summary: HDB flats became popular only after the 1968 CPF Act amendment allowed Singaporeans to use CPF funds for down payments and mortgage instalments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The popularity of HDB flats exploded only when the CPF Act was amended in 1968, allowing Singaporeans to use their CPF funds for down payments and mortgage instalments of HDB flats.

sections.label: WP Housing Motion and BTO flats
sections.summary: The WP made this point in its speeches during last year's Housing Motion, and the Prime Minister cited the $877,000 Ang Mo Kio five-room BTO flat in his 2023 National Day Rally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A point made by the WP in our speeches during the Housing Motion that was debated in Parliament last year, when we sought to bring focus to the People's Action Party's (PAP's) amended Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was not coincidental that the Prime Minister in his 2023 National Day Rally, referred to the now infamous $877,000 five-room BTO flat in Ang Mo Kio as an example of a BTO flat that should become slightly less expensive under the new Standard, Prime and Plus BTO classification system – thanks to added taxpayer subsidies.

sections.label: Local Qualifying Salary cap concerns
sections.summary: Business groups have expressed concerns about the new Local Qualifying Salary cap of $1,600, widely considered the de facto minimum wage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Business groups have expressed concerns about the new Local Qualifying Salary cap of $1,600, which is widely considered as the de facto minimum wage.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits or redundancy insurance
sections.summary: As the next step, Singapore should legislate retrenchment benefits or introduce redundancy insurance for these workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As the next step, Singapore should legislate retrenchment benefits or introduce redundancy insurance for these workers.

sections.label: Reasons employees leave jobs
sections.summary: Pay is one reason employees leave, while feeling unrecognised and a lack of career progression are two additional factors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While pay is one reason, feeling unrecognised and a lack of career progression, are the two additional factors that drive employees to leave.

sections.label: Citizens panel on employment resilience
sections.summary: A citizens panel on employment resilience under Forward Singapore noted workers did not proactively manage careers due to lack of awareness or daunting information.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A citizens panel on employment resilience concluded, as part of Forward Singapore, noted that many workers did not proactively manage their careers until a need arose – due to a lack of awareness of resources for upgrading; or to there being too much information that is too daunting to navigate.

sections.label: Sylvia Lim and SkillsFuture Credit
sections.summary: Aljunied GRC MP Sylvia Lim will speak more on this subject, and this year's Budget extends the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit for another year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Aljunied GRC Member of Parliament Ms Sylvia Lim will speak more on this subject.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This year's Budget sees the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit extended for another year.

sections.label: Finance Minister on uncertain outlook
sections.summary: The Finance Minister's speech assessed Singapore's uncertain outlook, including a darkened international outlook and a new era of conflict and confrontation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The segment of the Finance Minister's speech that stood out for me was the assessment of the uncertain outlook for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These include, and I quote: the international outlook has darkened dramatically; the post-Cold War era that fostered three decades of peace and stability is over; we are now in a new era of conflict and confrontation and there is no turning back; what can we expect in this new world?

sections.label: Security, support and transparency calls
sections.summary: Security agencies may face asymmetric challenges, Singaporeans must support uniformed personnel, and calls for transparency and civic participation must be accommodated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Our security agencies may be tested or challenged in ways that may not just be kinetic, but asymmetric, and we cannot afford to fall short.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: All Singaporeans must give our men and women in uniform our full support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But the call for a fair, inclusive and united Singapore must also accommodate and respond to citizen demands for greater transparency and civic participation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The WP has, on numerous occasions, proposed how these calls for greater transparency can be better addressed.

sections.label: Contested balanced Parliamentary system
sections.summary: A contested and balanced Parliamentary system with a robust opposition makes Singapore fairer, more inclusive, better, more confident and authentic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A Singapore with a contested and balanced Parliamentary system, with a robust opposition presence playing its role in making for a fair and inclusive society, and ultimately, what it does is that it makes us a better, more confident and an authentic Singapore.

sections.label: Enhanced Assurance Package
sections.summary: The $1.9 billion enhanced Assurance Package may seem like more of the same but is welcomed as more than that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The $1.9 billion enhanced Assurance Package (AP) may come across as "more of the same", but this is a much welcomed "more of the same", where it is actually more than "more of the same".

sections.label: Business tax rebate payouts
sections.summary: The 50% corporate tax rebate and Enterprise Financing Scheme may seem familiar, but minimum cash payouts of $2,000 to companies with a local employee are new.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: For the businesses, while the 50% corporate tax rebate and the Enterprise Financing Scheme, among others, may also come across as more of the same, the minimum cash payouts of $2,000 to all companies that employed at least one local employee is clearly a new feature and, if I remember correctly, first of its kind in our Budgets.

sections.label: Training allowance and SkillsFuture
sections.summary: A monthly training allowance of 50% of average income, capped at $3,000 over 24 months, buffers costs, and $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top-up for those 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The monthly training allowance, equivalent to 50% of one's average income, capped at $3,000 and over 24 months, helps to significantly buffer the economic costs for workers when they embark on career transition programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The $4,000 top-up of the SkillsFuture Credit for Singaporeans aged 40 and above is a sizeable uplift and a clear signaling in the way forward.

sections.label: Training allowances for full-time courses
sections.summary: Workers attending qualified full-time work courses can receive training allowances of up to $3,000 per month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Workers who wish to attend qualified full-time work courses, can also receive training allowances of up to $3,000 per month.

sections.label: EDB 2023 investment figures
sections.summary: In 2023, the EDB attracted FAI of $12.7 billion and TBE of $8.9 billion, expected to create over 20,000 jobs with $26.7 billion value-add.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: For example, in 2023, the EDB attracted FAI of $12.7 billion, TBE of $8.9 billion and these are expected to create more than 20,000 jobs with a projected value-add of $26.7 billion.

sections.label: Budget investments and Future Energy Fund
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister announced investments including $3 billion in RIE2025, $2 billion in the Financial Sector Development Fund, $100 million for broadband, and $5 billion for the Future Energy Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister announced a series of significant investment into our capabilities in this year's Budget; for example, the $3 billion in Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 (RIE2025), $2 billion in the Financial Sector Development Fund, $100 million to upgrade our Nationwide Broadband Network.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: To enhance our longer-term energy security, the Government will also inject an initial $5 billion to set up the Future Energy Fund.

sections.label: AI investments and BEPS tax
sections.summary: Investments will fund AI Centres of Excellences in Singapore and secure advanced AI chips, while Pillar 2 of BEPS requires a 15% global minimum effective tax on large MNEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The investments will be used to work with leading companies to set up AI Centres of Excellences in Singapore as well as secure the much needed advanced chips for AI development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Under Pillar 2 of BEPS, a global minimum effective tax of 15% is required to be applied to large MNEs.

sections.label: Additional corporate tax revenue
sections.summary: Using the revised FY2023 corporate tax revenue base of $28.4 billion, this would mean an additional $4 billion to $11 billion of revenue.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Using our revised FY2023 corporate tax revenue base of $28.4 billion, this would mean an additional $4 billion to $11 billion of revenue.

sections.label: BEPS 2.0 and Budget 2024 support
sections.summary: BEPS 2.0 is a key challenge for Singapore, and the speaker supports Budget 2024 measures enhancing the investment promotion toolkit through the Refundable Investment Credit and investments in workforce, innovation and infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The more important point is BEPS 2.0 is a key challenge for Singapore which we must navigate carefully.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: And which is I why, I support the Budget 2024 measures to enhance our investment promotion toolkit through the Refundable Investment Credit; as well as the various investments in our workforce, in innovation and in infrastructure.

sections.label: Budget 2024 assistance measures
sections.summary: The Budget includes assistance for cost-of-living pressures, a $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top up for those 40 and above, property tax easing, and a $1.3 billion Enterprise Support Package with a 50% corporate income tax rebate capped at $40,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: These include generous assistance to meet cost-of-living pressures to taking forward-looking steps to ensure Singapore and Singaporeans continue to thrive in a fast-changing economic and social environment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: There are significant progressive moves announced in this Budget, such as the SkillsFuture Credit top up of $4,000 for those 40 years and above to level up; as well as moves to better calibrate policy such as easing of property tax burden for many home owners who saw their tax bills spike.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Companies, especially SMEs, also stand to benefit from the $1.3 billion Enterprise Support Package with a slew of support measures, including the generous corporate income tax rebate of 50%, capped at $40,000 in the year of assessment FY2024.

sections.label: Budget 2024 capability development funding
sections.summary: Budget 2024 earmarked $13 billion towards capability development, including productivity, research and innovation, green transition and AI transformation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: We are not simply adopting new technologies; we are required to reshape our economic fabric.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, Budget 2024 rightly earmarked a substantial sum of $13 billion towards capability development – these include boosting productivity, research and innovation, green transition and AI transformation.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credit usage
sections.summary: Although SkillsFuture has been launched for close to 10 years, only three in 10 Singaporeans have used their SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, even though SkillsFuture has been launched for close to 10 years, only three in 10 Singaporeans have used their SkillsFuture credits.

sections.label: CPF payout replacement income
sections.summary: The new ERS payout would be about $3,300 monthly, a 63% replacement versus the 70% to 80% recommended, up from $2,530.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: If we consider the current median monthly income of about $5,200 for full-time working residents in the middle-income group, the estimated monthly payout under the new ERS would be approximately $3,300.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This represents a 63% replacement income versus the 70% to 80% recommended for middle-income earners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: This is a significant increase from the current monthly payout of $2,530, which only replaces about 49% of our median wage earner's income.

sections.label: FY2023 fiscal deficit
sections.summary: For FY2023, revenue rose 7.9% and surpassed $104 billion, but the fiscal deficit is revised to $3.6 billion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: For FY2023, despite a revenue increase exceeding expectations by 7.9% and surpassing $104 billion, the fiscal deficit for this year is, in fact, revised to $3.6 billion deficit.

sections.label: Real wage changes
sections.summary: After inflation, real wages rose 0.4% in 2022 but fell 4.5% in the first half of 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: After taking into account inflation, real wages rose by only 0.4% in 2022, but fell by 4.5% in the first half of 2023.

sections.label: Retail rent business costs
sections.summary: In the retail sector, rent constitutes about 30% of business costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In the retail sector, rent constitutes about 30% of the business costs.

sections.label: PSP Affordable Home Scheme
sections.summary: PSP proposed the Affordable Home Scheme, where HDB flat prices exclude land cost on first purchase, deferred upon sale.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP has proposed the Affordable Home Scheme in which HDB flat prices do not include the land cost component for home buyers upon first purchase, but deferred if and when they sell their flats.

sections.label: GST and healthcare expenditure
sections.summary: If healthcare expenditure hits $27 billion and is fully funded by GST, GST would have to rise about 3.5% by 2030 to about 12.5%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If healthcare expenditure hits $27 billion as expected and the increase is fully funded by GST, then GST would have to be raised by another 3.5% approximately by 2030, to reach about 12.5%.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme support
sections.summary: PSP supports the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme for Singaporeans aged 40 and above, but is disappointed that details of the temporary financial support scheme for the involuntarily unemployed are not ready.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP supports the introduction of the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme for Singaporeans aged 40 and above, which consists of a $4,000 credit, subsidies for another full-time diploma and training allowance for full-time trainees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: These policies will also enable our middle-aged workers to switch careers more easily and move into areas with better or more job opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We are, however, disappointed that details of the temporary financial support scheme for the involuntarily unemployed are still not ready.

sections.label: ITE Progression Award announcement
sections.summary: DPM Wong announced a new ITE Progression Award with a $5,000 top-up to Post-Secondary Education Accounts for ITE graduates enrolling in a diploma programme and a $10,000 CPF top-up on attaining polytechnic diplomas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: In his Budget speech, Deputy Prime Minister Wong announced his intention to ensure that the wages and career prospects of our ITE graduates should not be too far below their polytechnic- and university-going peers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: He then announced a new ITE Progression Award, which provides a $5,000 top-up to the Post-Secondary Education Accounts of ITE graduates who enrol in a diploma programme; and a $10,000 CPF top-up for ITE graduates when they attain polytechnic diplomas.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hazel Poa (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Today, about 4,000 ITE graduates – or about 28% of the annual ITE graduating cohort – qualify for polytechnics each year and about 4,000 ITE graduates enrol in the polytechnics each year.

sections.label: GST Voucher Fund and cost-of-living support
sections.summary: The $6 billion top-up to the GST Voucher Fund will secure permanent defrayment of GST expenses for lower- and middle-income households, with further support from various payments and rebates.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Lower- and middle-income households would be heartened that the $6 billion top-up to the GST Voucher Fund will secure the permanent defrayment of GST expenses for them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Many will receive further support from the Cost-of-Living Special Payment, the U-Save rebates and Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC) rebates; the additional $600 in Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers coming on the heels of the $500 recently disbursed, are appreciated.

sections.label: Healthcare subsidy thresholds and Silver Support
sections.summary: Raised per capita household income thresholds for healthcare and social support subsidy schemes will be welcomed, and the increase in the Silver Support Scheme is appreciated.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The raised per capita household income thresholds for healthcare and associated social support subsidy schemes, will be greatly welcomed by our families as more will be able to benefit from subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I also appreciate the increase in the Silver Support Scheme, which provides quarterly payments to seniors who had low incomes during their working years and have less family support.

sections.label: Australia right to disconnect legislation
sections.summary: Australia's recently enacted right to disconnect legislation amends the Fair Work Act to allow workers to refuse to monitor, read or respond to contact from their employer or a third party outside working hours, without penalty.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Take for example, the right to disconnect legislation recently enacted in Australia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Amendments made to the Fair Work Act will allow workers to refuse to monitor, read or respond to contact or attempted contact from their employer or a third-party outside of their working hours, without penalty.

sections.label: Litigation risk of right to disconnect
sections.summary: The Australian legislation gives workers an actionable right to disconnect, meaning more litigation and labour discord on something that may ultimately not be easy to prove.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The legislation in Australia gives the worker an actionable right to disconnect.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, this means more litigation, more labour discord on something that may ultimately not be easy to prove.

sections.label: Security industry officer shortage
sections.summary: The security industry has an estimated shortage of between eight and 18,000 officers at any one time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In the security industry there is an estimated shortage of between eight and 18,000 officers at any one time.

sections.label: Recognising workers beyond qualifications
sections.summary: Workers with lower academic qualifications are doing their part in the Singapore miracle and need recognition and reward, and the Deputy Prime Minister called for a broader definition of a good job.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The workers in these sectors may not hold very high academic qualifications but they are doing their part in the Singapore miracle and it is not a small part, and they need to be recognised and rewarded accordingly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I was very encouraged when I read Deputy Prime Minister Wong's speech at the IPS Singapore Perspectives Conference in January last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Amongst other things, the Deputy Prime Minister said that we should embrace a broader definition of a good job and recognise skills and competencies instead of overly focusing on paper qualifications.

sections.label: Budget support for PWMs and ITE graduates
sections.summary: The Budget contains measures to bolster the PWMs through the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme and to support ITE graduates through the Progression Award.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this Budget, there are also measures to bolster the PWMs through the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme as well as to support Institute of Education (ITE) graduates through the Progression Award.

sections.label: Security officer entry-level wage 2024
sections.summary: The PWMs have achieved significant wage increases but need to go further, with the prescribed entry-level security officer wage in 2024 at $2,650.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While the PWMs have achieved very significant wage increases that would have not occurred but for the PWMs, my view is that they need to go further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We can look at, for example, the prescribed entry-level security officer wage in 2024, which is $2,650.

sections.label: Security officer wages by 2028
sections.summary: By 2028, an entry-level security officer will earn a minimum basic wage of $3,530 or more, security supervisors $4,130 and senior security supervisors at least $4,430.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: By 2028, an entry-level security officer will earn a minimum basic wage of $3,530 or more; security supervisors will earn $4,130 and senior security supervisors at least $4,430.

sections.label: Wages compared with other countries
sections.summary: The average wages of cleaners, security officers and waste management personnel are not far from the average wage of a fresh university graduate in Sweden, Switzerland, Japan and Australia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: My research reveals that the average wages of cleaners, security officers and waste management personnel are not far from the average wage of a fresh university graduate in Sweden, Switzerland, Japan and Australia.

sections.label: Competitiveness, hard work, revenue growth
sections.summary: Singapore's prosperity requires hard work, and FY2023 operating revenues rose to $104.3 billion with corporate income taxes up 23%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The reality of maintaining Singapore’s competitiveness and our prosperity is that, if we want to continue to live well, we must be prepared to work hard.

sentences.speaker: Mr Raj Joshua Thomas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And those who work hard should expect that they will get the rewards and respect that enable them to live well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Overall operating revenues increased by $13.3 billion in FY2023 compared to a year ago to $104.3 billion, and this is also $7.6 billion higher than projected operating revenues first revealed in Budget 2023 last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: What was most impressive was the 23% jump in corporate income taxes in FY2023, even after a sharp jump of 27% the year before, with corporate income taxes set to be sustained at record high levels of around $28 billion.

sections.label: FY2023 deficit and Majulah Package
sections.summary: FY2023 is projected in deficit largely due to special transfers including the $7.5 billion Majulah Package Fund; without it there would be a $3.9 billion surplus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the overall fiscal position for FY2023 is still projected to be in deficit, this was largely due to an increase in special transfers, chief of which is the recent inclusion of the $7.5 billion Majulah Package Fund, without which FY2023 would have seen a $3.9 billion surplus instead.

sections.label: Raising gambling duties
sections.summary: Gambling duties unchanged since 2014 leave room to raise them, which could also serve a deterrent function.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Given that gambling duties have been unchanged since 2014, there is room to look into raising the relevant gambling duties, which could also serve a deterrent function.

sections.label: Corporate income tax rebate YA2024
sections.summary: A 50% corporate income tax rebate of tax payable will be granted to all taxpaying companies, tax resident or not, for YA 2024.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Similarly, on corporate income tax (CIT), a CIT rebate of 50% of the corporate tax payable will be granted to all taxpaying companies, whether tax resident or not, for YA 2024.

sections.label: SME tax before and after rebates
sections.summary: An SME with $300,000 chargeable income would pay close to $34,000 before rebates, an 11.2% effective rate, versus around $25,000 or 8.4% under prior rules.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: For an SME making $300,000 in chargeable income for example, total corporate income tax paid before any rebates would be close to $34,000 or an effective tax rate of 11.2%, compared to around $25,000 or an effective tax rate of 8.4% based on prior rules.

sections.label: OECD global minimum tax gains
sections.summary: An OECD working paper finds the global minimum tax can raise US$155 to US$192 billion yearly, with investment hubs including Singapore gaining most.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To put into context my question, the OECD has published a working paper earlier this year, which finds that the global minimum tax “can raise between US$155 to US$192 billion of additional CIT revenues per year, with revenue gains accruing to all jurisdiction groups”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Moreover, estimated participating countries categorised as “investment hubs,” which includes Singapore, would have the largest expected gains from the reforms, with corporate income tax revenues rising from 14% minimum to up to 34%.

sections.label: CPF LIFE interest pooling
sections.summary: From payout age, interest earned on RA funds is pooled under CPF LIFE and not paid to beneficiaries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is also true that from the age of 55 to, say, the payout age of 65, these RA funds continue to earn the same interest rate floor of 4% as with the SA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But unbeknownst to many, from the moment payouts commence, any interest earned will not accrue to the CPF holder, but it is pooled together under CPF LIFE for all members.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: An FAQ by the CPF Board says it best, that interest earned on CPF LIFE premium is not included as part of the amount paid to beneficiaries when one passes away.

sections.label: CPF doubling time comparison
sections.summary: Using GIC's 6.9% returns, CPF doubles in about 10 years; at the 2.5% OA rate, 29 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: As I have shared, based on the 20-year nominal returns of the GIC portfolio of 6.9% and the CPF-OA rate of 2.5%, based on a simple rule of 72, the number of years it takes for our CPF monies to double goes from about 10 years based on GIC’s returns, to 29 years based on the prevailing OA rate.

sections.label: Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme call
sections.summary: The speaker urges urgent implementation of LIRS, citing panel views on CPFIS limitations and delay costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: If for some reason the Government is still adamant that we are unwilling or unable to allow Singaporeans to share in the fund management expertise and returns of the GIC, then the least we can do is to urgently implement the Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme (LIRS), something which I have been repeating in each of the last three years so that we can better support Singaporeans' retirement needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To quote then Minister Lim: "These additional options will help address the concerns some Singaporeans may have with regard to the rising cost of living in retirement and the desire for higher expected investment returns for those who had to take on some investment risk." One of our fellow MPs today, Mr Saktiandi Supaat, was a part of the CPF Advisory Panel too, where Chairman Prof Tan Chor Chuan articulated the limitations of the CPF Investment Scheme (CPFIS) and put it so aptly, that "the Panel believes that there is a need to provide an additional investment avenue that can better help such CPF members earn higher expected returns than the CPF interest rates in a simpler way than CPFIS." The big question I have is, when will the Government finally be ready to roll this out?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I hope the Government is cognisant that the longer the delay, the higher the opportunity cost and real cost to Singaporeans' retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: To conclude, Mr Speaker, I appreciate the Government providing for one off goodies and handouts to Singaporeans and Singapore companies, on the back of yet another record high operating revenues, which were $13 billion higher compared to a year ago.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, it is important that we put in place structural levers in our system as opposed to relying on one-off schemes and I have suggested changes to our personal and corporate income tax systems to illustrate this point.

sections.label: ABSD refund for senior singles
sections.summary: Government now allows single Singaporeans above 55 to claim ABSD refund on a second property when downsizing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Many Singaporeans aspire to own a private property because in some ways, it is an investment with high potential returns that could be unlocked during their silver years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government now allows senior single Singaporeans above the age of 55 years old to claim for a refund of the ABSD on a second private property when they are downsizing.

sections.label: ABSD refund for younger singles
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the ABSD refund scheme could extend to younger single Singaporeans buying a smaller second property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In the same vein, I would like to ask if the Government would consider extending the same ABSD refund scheme to younger single Singaporeans who are buying a smaller second private property to stay in, if they sell their first property within six months of acquiring their second private property.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit mid-career top-up
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up and Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy for a diploma programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In particular, I welcome the $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-Career) top-up and the Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy for another publicly funded full-time diploma programme.

sections.label: Mid-career diploma teaching and subsidy
sections.summary: The passage urges that mid-career diploma programmes be designed and taught differently, and that the Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy be extended to part-time diploma courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Similar to how the teaching methods and teaching styles must differ between in a Masters programme and an undergraduate programme, for example, the diploma programme for mid-career Singaporeans must be designed and taught differently as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I would also urge the Government to extend the Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy to part-time diploma courses as well, not just full-time ones.

sections.label: Personal learning devices for primary students
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOE would provide personal learning devices to primary school children, extending the secondary school procurement framework and financial support schemes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While MOE committed to providing PLDs to all secondary students by end-2021 to be used in tandem with the national e-learning platform Student-Learning-Space (SLS), would MOE now not also consider providing PLDs to children in primary schools as well?

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With the procurement framework of PLDs for secondary schools in place, it is now a matter of extending the same procurement framework and financial support schemes to students in our primary schools as well.

sections.label: Ageing in dignity by 2030
sections.summary: The passage states that Singapore is due to become a super-aged society by 2030 and that ageing in dignity is a foremost concern for many Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: With Singapore due to become a super-aged society by 2030, ageing in dignity is one of the foremost concerns for many Singaporeans.

sections.label: Localised ecosystems for seniors
sections.summary: The passage hopes the Government will build robust localised ecosystems allowing seniors to age with dignity, beyond Medisave top-ups and Silver Support Scheme support.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Beyond providing top-ups to Medisave and direct financial support through the Silver Support Scheme, I also hope that the Government can also work towards building robust localised ecosystems that allow our seniors to age with dignity.

sections.label: Multi-tier unemployment support proposal
sections.summary: The passage proposes a multi-tier unemployment support approach balancing personal responsibility, insurance risk-pooling and Government support, with a basic payout funded by unemployment insurance through CPF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: Factoring in the views of my residents, I propose a multi-tier approach towards unemployment support that balances three critical pillars of social support: one, a strong sense of personal responsibility; two, efficient risk-pooling through insurance; three, sufficient Government support, which is largely, let us not forget, largely funded by our taxes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I hope we can see a basic and not gold-plated unemployment payout for several months with an upper limit on one's lifetime, funded by unemployment insurance and, hopefully, we can pay for this insurance through the CPF.

sections.label: Options to help cash flow
sections.summary: The passage offers options such as freezing housing loans, healthcare, insurance premiums, taxes and fees, providing Government transfers ahead of schedule, and borrowing against CPF monies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: To do so, we can offer them these options: fully or partially freezing housing loans and majority of healthcare, insurance premiums, taxes and fees, for a limited time to help with their cash flow, providing Government transfers, such as GST rebates ahead of schedule, that means, they can take their subsidies and transfers ahead of other Singaporeans and allowing them to borrow against their own CPF monies for those Singaporeans with healthy CPF balances already.

sections.label: Top-up for industry downsizing
sections.summary: Speaker hopes Government will top up monthly assistance for workers in industries undergoing major downsizing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: If there are specific industries or large companies that are going through a major downsizing, I hope the Government can step up to top up the monthly assistance, perhaps through a larger or longer payout, because when there is a large number of people exiting one industry, not everybody can quickly move into another industry.

sections.label: PAP Seniors Group thanks Government
sections.summary: PAP Seniors Group thanks Government for an A-plus Budget for seniors and for acting on seniors' CPF, estates and home-care issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: On behalf of PAP Seniors Group, I would like to thank the Government for delivering an A-plus Budget for seniors and for taking onboard many of the suggestions from PAP SG MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: I am also heartened that the Government is moving decisively on issues that I have spoken about over the years: seniors' CPF contribution rates, making our estates more senior-friendly and encouraging home-care services.

sections.label: Scaling up Age Well SG sandbox
sections.summary: Speaker calls for quickly scaling up Age Well SG's caregiving home-care sandbox.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: First, quickly scaling up Age Well SG's caregiving home-care sandbox.

sections.label: Cost-of-living offsets and foreign hires
sections.summary: Speaker seeks more cost-of-living offsets for seniors and families, and more foreign hires in exchange for flexible work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: First of all, I hope to see the Government provide more cost-of-living offsets in the next Budget, not just in this, especially to help our seniors and families, including those who are asset-rich and cash-poor, especially retirees living in the private estates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry (Kebun Baru)
sentences.text: One, to reduce the manpower shortage, can we allow our companies to hire more foreigners, at a reasonable levy, in exchange for them creating even more flexible work arrangement opportunities, which will benefit our seniors, stay-at-home mums and caregivers?

sections.label: 2023 revenue and Budget surplus
sections.summary: Higher 2023 operating revenue plus NIRC gave over $30 billion surplus, enabling a record capital transfer to endowment and trust funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Operating revenue in 2023 was larger than the original estimate by $8 billion because of the tax increases announced in 2022, high inflation and high property prices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This $8 billion excess revenue, together with the $23.5 billion Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) for 2024, contributed to surplus Budget resources of more than $30 billion to be allocated in this Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: As a result, the Government was able to make a record capital transfer of more than $30 billion to top up existing endowment and trust funds and create some new ones.

sections.label: Closing CPF Special Account
sections.summary: The Government has decided to close the Special Account for CPF members above 55 years old.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Government has also decided to close the SA for CPF members above 55 years old.

sections.label: PSP permanent scheme approach
sections.summary: PSP's permanent scheme approach would consolidate over 60 Government schemes into a few permanent national schemes with minimum support and work incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: PSP’s permanent scheme approach will streamline and consolidate the Government’s 60 over schemes into a few permanent, national schemes which are easy to understand, provides a minimum level of support and an incentive mechanism for Singaporeans to work towards bettering themselves.

sections.label: Deferment of land cost
sections.summary: The speaker recommended deferring land cost from HDB flat pricing under the Affordable Homes Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: First and foremost, I have recommended the deferment of land cost from HDB flat pricing under the Affordable Homes Scheme (AHS).

sections.label: Wage, wage scheme, health insurance
sections.summary: PSP recommends a minimum gross monthly wage of about $2,200, a permanent Progressive Wage Scheme, and a Government-funded National Health Insurance Scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: After ensuring a minimum gross monthly wage of about $2,200, we would like to recommend the Government to put in a permanent Progressive Wage Scheme to incentivise all Singaporean workers to continuously upskill towards higher gross monthly wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, we have urged the Government to set up a National Health Insurance Scheme funded by it rather than having Singaporeans pay for their MediShield and CareShield premiums.

sections.label: Streamlining social welfare structure
sections.summary: PSP says social welfare can be streamlined to focus on a smaller needy group, with permanent schemes giving certainty and incentives, without significantly more fiscal resources.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Our social welfare and security structure can also be streamlined and consolidated to focus on a much smaller group of needy Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: This is especially important as it ensures that this smaller group, who still need further help beyond that provided under the permanent schemes, receive the assistance they need expeditiously.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: The latter empowers Singaporeans with the certainty of help when they need it and encourages them to strive for higher goals with incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: PSP estimated that the shift to the permanent scheme approach will not consume significantly more fiscal resources – because the Government already has more than 60 schemes in place and has locked away tens of billions of dollars in endowment and trust funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: PSP believes that we can do a lot more to improve the well-being of our citizens, work to combat future challenges, such as climate change and, provide support to worthy humanitarian causes abroad.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai
sentences.text: As owners of one of the largest sovereign wealth in the world, Singaporeans deserve better policies that can lead to better lives and a more secure future.

sections.label: ITE and SkillsFuture programmes
sections.summary: The passage welcomes DPM Wong's announcement of the ITE Progression Award and SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme for Singaporeans aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong's announcement for young ITE graduates to pursue diploma qualifications through the ITE Progression Award and the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme for Singaporeans aged 40 and above, is something that is welcomed.

sections.label: Public transport fare support
sections.summary: The passage notes public transport fares rose 10 to 11 cents per trip in September 2023 and suggests extending targeted support beyond PCHI of $1,600 or less.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Even for public transport, fares have risen by 10 cents to 11 cents per trip in September 2023 and similar increases can be expected in the coming years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: More importantly, may I suggest that the Government consider extending targeted support for public transport, beyond those whose per capita household income (PCHI) is $1,600 or less?

sections.label: URA rental index surge
sections.summary: The URA Rental Index for private residential properties rose 35.3% from Q1 2022 to Q4 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Urban Redevelopment Authority (URA) Rental Index for private residential properties, saw a 35.3% surge from Q1 2022 to Q4 2023.

sections.label: CPF Special Account removal
sections.summary: Removing the Special Account for those above 55 ends a shielding hack, moving excess funds above the ERS to the OA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In relation to the removal of the Special Account for those above age 55, I understand that such a move will get rid of a "shielding" hack – where wealthier CPF members are able to keep an amount that is more than their ERS in their Special and Retirement Accounts and earn the higher 4% interest on the whole of that amount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But now that the Special Account will be closed, any excess funds above the ERS will be deposited back into the OA that only earns an interest rate of 2.5%.

sections.label: Support for involuntarily unemployed
sections.summary: The speaker supports in principle the temporary financial support scheme for the involuntarily unemployed announced by Lawrence Wong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: For those who are unemployed – not by choice – I am supportive in principle of the temporary financial support scheme that Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong had announced for the involuntarily unemployed.

sections.label: Changi Airport cargo and passengers
sections.summary: Changi Airport's cargo flows dipped 6% versus 2022, while airports like Incheon close the passenger gap to Changi.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Possibly, it could be discussed in the COS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: But I note that Changi Airport's cargo flows dipped 6% compared with 2022, while other airports, like Incheon, are closing the gap to Changi, in terms of passenger flows.

sections.label: Refundable Investment Credit details
sections.summary: The Refundable Investment Credit is consistent with Global Anti-Base Erosion Rules, giving up to 50% support per qualifying expenditure category.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The new Refundable Investment Credit, based on the presently available information and announced by the Deputy Prime Minister, will be consistent with the Global Anti-Base Erosion Rules for Qualified Refundable Tax Credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Companies will be able to receive up to 50% of support of each qualifying expenditure category, including capital expenditure, manpower and training costs, freight and logistics costs.

sections.label: UK AI skills package
sections.summary: The UK announced a £118 million skills package including a visa scheme for AI researchers and relocation grants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Thereafter, the UK government announced a £118 million skills package that includes a new visa scheme for AI researchers to be brought to the UK at the early stages of their career, as well as grants to help AI workers meet the costs of relocating to the UK.

sections.label: AI grants for Singapore companies
sections.summary: Asks whether grants will exist for Singapore companies adopting AI solutions or doing AI-related research soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As part of our $1 billion effort to develop AI computation, talent and industry in the next five years, will there be grants for Singapore companies adopting AI-based solutions or engaging in AI-related research in the near future?

sections.label: Singapore healthcare spending increase
sections.summary: Singapore's healthcare investment rose from $789 per capita in 2011 to $2,674 today, a 338% increase over 10 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Singapore has continued to invest more into healthcare, to take care of Singaporeans, from $789 per capita in 2011, to $2,674 per capita today, a 338% increase over the last 10 years.

sections.label: Singapore centenarian numbers doubling
sections.summary: Singapore had 700 centenarians in 2010 and more than 1,500 in 2020, more than double.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2010, there were 700 centenarians and, in 2020, there are more than 1,500, more than double.

sections.label: ASEAN foreign direct investment 2022
sections.summary: In 2022, ASEAN's foreign direct investments reached a high of $224 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2022, ASEAN's foreign direct investments (FDI) have reached a high of $224 billion.

sections.label: Singapore FDI share of GDP
sections.summary: In 2022, Singapore's FDI equals 31.7% of Singapore's nominal GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2022, Singapore's FDI equals to 31.7% of Singapore's nominal GDP.

sections.label: Spending per primary school student
sections.summary: In 2013, Singapore spent and invested $8,550 for every primary school student.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In 2013, Singapore spent and invested $8,550 for every primary school student.

sections.label: Singapore global talent ranking
sections.summary: INSEAD's index ranks Singapore first in global knowledge and skills and third in vocational and technical skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: According to INSEAD's annual Global Talent Competitiveness Index, Singapore ranked number one in global knowledge and skills, which included management and communication abilities; and third in vocational and technical skills.

sections.label: Gaza population age
sections.summary: Forty percent of Gaza's population is 14 years and below.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Forty percent of Gaza's population is 14 years and below.

sections.label: Ukraine male life expectancy
sections.summary: In Ukraine, male life expectancy fell from 67 years before the war to 57 years after.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: In Ukraine, the male life expectancy has decreased from 67 years before the war to 57 years after, or right now.

sections.label: OpenAI Sora video platform
sections.summary: OpenAI announced Sora, an AI platform that turns typed text prompts into videos indistinguishable from Hollywood and smaller studio output.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: A tech company which is already changing the world – a tech company called OpenAI, which brought you ChatGPT not too long ago.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: That company announced a new AI platform, called Sora.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Sora allows you to key in text – type in some text, a prompt – and it can produce videos, which are indistinguishable from what Hollywood can produce today and what smaller studios can produce.

sections.label: Sora announcement timeframe
sections.summary: Within 10 months, OpenAI had announced the Sora platform-produced AI-generated video.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Within 10 months, OpenAI had announced the Sora platform-produced AI-generated video.

sections.label: Subsidy for older Singaporeans
sections.summary: A new Budget subsidy lets Singaporeans aged 40 and above pursue another full-time diploma in higher education.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, we have to accept the world as it is, the way the world is going to be and look after, support, empower and uplift our people.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This is why the new subsidy for Singaporeans age 40 and above to pursue another full-time diploma in higher education – this new subsidy in the Budget, that is why it is so important.

sections.label: Future Energy Fund and hydrogen hubs
sections.summary: The $5 billion Future Energy Fund lets Singapore move quickly on low-carbon technologies to secure energy and water security.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, because in a market where you may not have room for too many hydrogen hubs, it matters whether you are first mover, second mover or too late to move.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: So, the Future Energy Fund in this year's Budget – the Future Energy Fund, with its initial injection of $5 billion is a significant decisive move.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It will allow Singapore to move quickly and seize opportunities in the energy sector, especially new low-carbon technologies – that in the future will help us secure our energy supply and, in turn, secure our water security for another generation.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Having a stronger supply of low-carbon energy will also help Singapore with our AI ambitions.

sections.label: Onshore data centres and AI ambition
sections.summary: Derisking and decoupling make it sensible to have more data centres and computing power onshore, requiring low-carbon energy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: But in a world where major economies sometimes do not get along; in a world where, sometimes, you have derisking or decoupling, it makes sense to have more of those data centres, more of that computing power onshore in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And having low-carbon energy – a greener energy future – more secure energy supply will be key for that AI ambition as well.

sections.label: Proposed SG Togetherness Office
sections.summary: The passage proposes an SG Togetherness Office in the Prime Minister's Office Strategy Group to assess policies' impact on social togetherness.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: These are questions that have to be asked not just for these policies but in every policy in Government, moving ahead.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: And so, I suggest for this Government to set up an SG Togetherness Office (SGTO).

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: I know it sounds like more alphabet soup, amidst many acronyms, but SG Togetherness Office, the SGTO – I suggest for this Government to set up the SG Togetherness Office which can be part of the Prime Minister's Office Strategy Group (PMOSG), which has approached major issues, like climate change, in the same coordinated, whole-of-Government way.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: The SG Togetherness Office could have an inter-ministry steering committee, chaired by a senior member of Cabinet, a Co-ordinating Minister or a Deputy Prime Minister, with that experience of Ministries and connectivity and links to help drive the agenda.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: It should have a secretariat, a team of public officers actively looking at the net impact on social togetherness for every policy and every programme across Government.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: This ethos of strengthening social togetherness and social cohesion, strengthening our social reserves, safeguarding our social reserves, has to be looked at with the same discipline, deliberation and attention that we give to the fiscal bottom line and to Singapore's financial reserves.

sections.label: Enterprise Support Package for SMEs
sections.summary: The Enterprise Support Package provides CIT support, SME loan increases, and funds for FinTech and green finance capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Enterprise Support Package, with the 50% Corporate Income Tax (CIT) and minimum $2,000 cash payout signals that the Government is serious about supporting SMEs through its cost challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Targeted support for SMEs is provided for through the permanent increase of the SME Working Capital Loan, capped to $500,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The $2 billion top-up to the Financial Sector Development Fund and the new Refundable Investment Credit will enable Singapore to build capabilities in new areas like FinTech and green finance and attract investment in high-value and substantive economic activities.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Mark accreditation
sections.summary: SBF manages the Progressive Wage Mark scheme and has accredited close to 4,500 companies with trade associations and chambers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Today, SBF manages the Progressive Wage Mark accreditation scheme and has partnered trade associations and chambers (TACs), like the Association for Catering Professionals, the Singapore Fashion Council, the Restaurant Association of Singapore and the Environmental Management Association of Singapore, to encourage companies to be part of this movement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am proud to share that close to 4,500 companies have since been accredited.

sections.label: AI strategy and SME sandbox funding
sections.summary: Budget 2024 allocates $1 billion for National AI Strategy 2.0 and $5 billion for the Future Energy Fund.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The allocation of $1 billion for National AI Strategy 2.0 and $5 billion for the Future Energy Fund in Budget 2024 highlights the Government efforts of fostering growth in these new sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The recent introduction of the ESG/IMDA AI Sandbox, which aims to involve 300 SMEs to participate, is a testament to ensure SMEs remain at the forefront of innovation.

sections.label: Labour growth and job targets
sections.summary: A recommendation calls for responsible labour growth to create 8,400 manufacturing, 2,000 logistics and 1,600 environmental services jobs amid a declining resident labour force.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Our third recommendation is a continual call for responsible labour growth to sustain Singapore's growth ambitions According to the Singapore 2030 vision and updated Industry Transformation Maps, we aim to create 8,400 jobs in manufacturing, 2,000 in logistics and 1,600 in environmental services, among others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mark Lee (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This is against the backdrop of a declining resident labour force, which saw a reduction of 1,800 last year.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Given these factors, I would like to call on the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) not to maintain and not tighten the foreign worker quota and foreign worker levy in sectors that are not favoured by Singaporeans, especially for the next three years where the world economy is very uncertain.

sections.label: S Pass pay increase example
sections.summary: A motor insurance claims executive working in hot and humid workshops will see his pay rise from about $3,400 to $4,200 upon S Pass renewal, almost 24%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: For example, a motor insurance claims executive who consistently works in hot and humid workshops will see his pay increase from about $3,400 to $4,200 upon renewal of his S Pass and this translates to an almost 24%-pay increase.

sections.label: CDC Vouchers and assistance criteria
sections.summary: The speaker proposes doubling CDC Vouchers for every three registered Singaporeans in HDB flats and asks MOH and MSF to incorporate inflation or CPI into income criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: The only setback is that CDC Vouchers are given to each household, regardless of family size.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Hence, I propose that the Ministry of Finance consider doubling the quantum of CDC Vouchers for every three registered Singaporeans residing in HDB flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Lastly, I would like MOH and MSF to consider incorporating inflation or the Consumer Price Index, or CPI, into the formula used to determine the income criteria for various Government financial assistance schemes.

sections.label: Real income decline in 2023
sections.summary: The real income of Singaporeans declined by 2.2% in 2023 even though nominal income increased.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In fact, the real income of Singaporeans has declined by 2.2% in 2023, even though the nominal income has increased.

sections.label: Yearly review of assistance criteria
sections.summary: The speaker appeals to MOH and MSF to incorporate the price index into income criteria for financial assistance and to review it yearly or quarterly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: But in the current high inflation rate environment, where periodic reviews are done every few years disadvantage low-wage Singaporeans very greatly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: Hence, I appeal to MOH and MSF to incorporate the price index into the income criteria for determining financial assistance to provide for low-income families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: In short, the periodic review should occur yearly or even quarterly, rather than once in a few years' time.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme
sections.summary: The Budget introduces the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, including a $4,000 SkillsFuture credit top-up in May, to support mid-career workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As such, the Budget packages announced that can affect some of their career trajectory and opportunities are of great interest to them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am delighted to hear that the Government is introducing the new SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme to better support mid-career workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This includes a $4,000 top-up SkillsFuture credit in May to encourage more mid-career workers to refresh their skills and progress in their careers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As data published from SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) last year showed, across all ages, seven in 10 Singaporeans have not yet used their SkillsFuture Credit since the scheme started in 2015.

sections.label: Earn and Save Bonus
sections.summary: The Earn and Save Bonus provides up to $1,000 annually to help young seniors accumulate more retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: One of these is the Earn and Save Bonus of up to $1,000 annually to help young seniors accumulate more retirement savings.

sections.label: CPF transfers and PPHS voucher
sections.summary: The speaker urges clearer CPF Retirement Account transfer explanations and welcomes the one-year PPHS (Open Market) Voucher for eligible families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Although the Enhanced Retirement Scheme is helpful for those seeking higher CPF retirement payouts, I urge the CPF Board to highlight and explain the policies for transfers into Retirement Account clearer and to work with HDB to advise those who have not yet settled their housing needs, to be more mindful of the amounts to be transferred into their Retirement Account.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Lastly, I would like to speak about the aspirations of our young couples and families, and how they can be better supported to achieve their dreams of home ownership and starting their own family.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government has introduced the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme or PPHS (Open Market) Voucher in this Budget for one year to support eligible families to rent a HDB flat in the open market.

sections.label: Extending PPHS voucher
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the PPHS (Open Market) Voucher could extend to couples still balloting for a flat, especially those expecting a first baby.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Could the Government consider extending the new PPHS (Open Market) Voucher also to couples who have been applying, but have yet to be successful in balloting for a new flat, especially those who are expecting their first baby?

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to a survey done by Channel NewsAsia and YouGov in 2023, 52% of those below 35 years old cited the affordability of raising a child in Singapore as the main reason for not wanting to have one soon.

sections.label: Democracy and bipartisanship
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Wong said both sides stand for a maturing democracy, a serious Government and Opposition, rejecting populism and political opportunism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong characterised it as follows: "Both sides of the House, we stand for a democracy that is maturing, a serious Government and a serious Opposition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But we say no to populism and political opportunism ever taking root in this House and in Singapore." This was a laudable bipartisan moment.

sections.label: Dutch Freedom Party gains
sections.summary: In November 2023, the far-right Freedom Party won the Netherlands election by a wide margin after anti-immigration campaigning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In November 2023, in the Netherlands, the Freedom Party, a far-right political party that fanned Islamophobia and anti-immigration sentiments amongst its people, with promises to de-Islamicise the country, made huge electoral gains and was the clear winner by a wide margin.

sections.label: Hugo Chavez Venezuela oil wealth
sections.summary: In 1998 Hugo Chavez came to power after promising to use Venezuela's oil wealth to reduce poverty and inequality.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In 1998, the late Mr Hugo Chavez, a charismatic Venezualuan leftist leader, came to power after promising to use Venezuala's vast oil wealth to reduce poverty and inequality.

sections.label: Slowing reserves growth advocated
sections.summary: Both hon Members advocated slowing the growth of reserves so more money can be spent on these areas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Both hon Members advocated for the slowing of the growth of reserves so that more money can be spent on these areas.

sections.label: Government rejecting more reserves spending
sections.summary: The Government stated the reserves provide passive income for Annual Budgets and must grow given unique vulnerabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: To explain its hard choice in rejecting even more spending of the income from the reserves, the Government has stated that the reserves provide substantial "passive income" for expenditure in the Annual Budgets and given our unique vulnerabilities, we need to grow the reserves to ensure that we have a chance of overcoming what future challenge that may come our way.

sections.label: Returns from reserves projection
sections.summary: He projected returns from reserves at about 4%, with 2% for the Budget and 2% for reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Hon Members may recall he asked us to take out the back of our envelopes and follow him in doing the sums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: He projected that the returns from the reserves at about 4%; he then said if we were to spend 2% for the Budget, that means 2% for the reserves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, the reserves will grow at a rate of 2% per year and that more or less, keeps up with the GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: So, we roughly know what is the band of the NIRC which has remained stable and contributes about one-fifth of our revenue.

sections.label: NIRC amount estimated for planning
sections.summary: The NIRC amount can be estimated, which is important for Budget planning.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: This is something which, as we all know, the Government has a conscientious objection to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: But most importantly, as I said earlier, the NIRC amount can be estimated and that is the important part for Budget planning.

sections.label: Monies committed for programmes
sections.summary: The $1.5 billion committed for these programmes is public knowledge, per Deputy Prime Minister Wong's announcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The amount of monies committed for these programmes is a matter of public knowledge – $1.5 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong, in his announcement, said that the package was designed to fully cover the increase in cost of living for lower-income households and to cover more than half the increase in the cost of living for middle-income households.

sections.label: Conscientious objection and NIRC
sections.summary: The speaker links conscientious objection to Government arguments on national reserves and says NIRC can already be calculated for the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: The reference to conscientious objection is really the arguments made by the Government in the Motion on national reserves which I am sure the hon Leader of Opposition is familiar with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: But more importantly, I made the point that for the purposes of the Budget, if one can calculate the NIRC already and I made reference to the hon Prime Minister's masterclass, in relation to how the reserves are projected to grow and the fact that the NIRC contributions are relatively stable.

sections.label: Opposition housing spending framework
sections.summary: The speaker outlines a framework requiring an Opposition Member to identify a programme, state its cost and take a position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: If we were to go through the analytical framework that I have suggested, the point is really about a Member of the Opposition, for example, articulating that even more houses should be built than what the Government is proposing, then what really needs to be done is to, first, identify the programme, highlight and find out how much exactly is being spent or committed for the purposes of building X number of flats, for example, and then also, in the same process, nail his colours to the mast and say exactly what he stands for in relation to the number of flats that is to be built, why is this important and then deal with the financial issues by reference to the allocation of the spend for the other aspects of the Budget as well.

sections.label: Opposition schemes and affordability
sections.summary: The speaker notes other Members proposing schemes like Carefare and PAP Members raising an affordability crisis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: Similarly, when other Members on the other side say we want to introduce a scheme, such as Carefare, or they speak of — nobody said cost of living crisis, but I heard affordability crisis today by PAP Members.

sections.label: ForwardSG $40 billion commitment
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether a Government commitment to spend $40 billion on ForwardSG initiatives should be laid out earlier.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: In the case of a commitment made by the Government, for example, to spend $40 billion up to the end of the decade for ForwardSG initiatives, should these also be laid out earlier?

sections.label: Stable NIRC and Budget share
sections.summary: The speaker says NIRC in the Budget has been relatively stable, with 20 cents of every dollar spent coming from it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
