sentences.text: Even if we were to put aside the assumptions of growth, the fact is that the NIRC, which is reflected in the Budget, has been relatively stable and it is now for every dollar that has been spent, 20 cents comes from NIRC.

sections.label: Information to calculate revenue
sections.summary: The speaker says all information needed to calculate revenue is available, including NIRC and operating revenue expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: Because all the information needed to calculate revenue is there, in terms of NIRC, in terms of the operating revenue expenditure which falls more or less within a defined variance as well.

sections.label: Budget revenue and expenditure
sections.summary: The Government sets out operating revenue and proposed operating expenditure, with constitutional requirements for a balanced Budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: As far as the Government is concerned, it puts out the operating revenue, it puts out the proposed operating expenditure and there are, of course, constitutional requirements to make sure that the Budget is balanced and it is against that backdrop that we can do the analysis as to whether the proposals meet the aspirations or the requirements of Singapore and Singaporeans for now and the future.

sections.label: Budget Statement contributions projection
sections.summary: Contributions are set out in the Budget Statement with a projection made by reference to a framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: So, that is something that is being set out in the Budget Statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
sentences.text: So, as far as contributions are concerned, of course, there is a certain projection and is made by reference to a certain framework.

sections.label: Medium-term outlook small surplus
sections.summary: Taking a medium- to long-term outlook while expecting a small surplus of $800 million reflects a privileged financial position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The fact that we can take a medium- to long-term outlook and yet expect a small surplus of $800 million reflects our privileged financial position.

sections.label: Survey of persons with disabilities
sections.summary: The speaker collected experiences and thoughts of 136 PwDs aged 15 to 35 through an online survey over a few weeks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, I collected the experiences and thoughts of 136 PwDs between the ages of 15 and 35 through a public consultation in the form of an online survey over the course of a few weeks.

sections.label: Autistic students in mainstream schools
sections.summary: MOE states 18% of students with autism from SPED schools continued in mainstream secondary schools after PSLE in three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to MOE, in the past three years, 18% of students with autism from SPED schools continued their education in mainstream secondary schools after passing the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE).

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A further 18 SPED school students with autism transferred midway to mainstream schools after being assessed to be suitable.

sections.label: Public transport use by disabled
sections.summary: In the survey, 63% of those with physical disabilities use public transport two days or less a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In my survey, 63% of those with physical disabilities said they use public transport two days or less in a week.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Forty-two percent of this group rarely uses or totally avoids using public transport during peak periods.

sections.label: ActiveSG gyms inclusivity target
sections.summary: SportSG is on track to make all 27 ActiveSG gyms inclusive by 2026.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, I understand that SportSG is on track to make all 27 ActiveSG gyms inclusive by 2026.

sections.label: PwDs wanting own homes
sections.summary: Eighty-one percent of surveyed PwDs said they wish to buy their own house in future.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Eighty-one percent of the PwDs I surveyed, said that they wish to buy their own house in future.

sections.label: Disability pay gap and WFL
sections.summary: MOM reports a 13% median pay gap for PMETs with disabilities, a one-to-four part-time ratio, and the WFL excludes reasonable accommodation provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to MOM, there is a 13% median pay gap between PMETs with disabilities and those without.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The ratio of part-time to full-time employed PwDs in the workforce is approximately one to four.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While I acknowledge the Government's acceptance of the Tripartite Committee's final recommendations, which excludes reasonable accommodation provisions from the initial form of the upcoming Workplace Fairness Legislation (WFL), this decision poses significant questions.

sections.label: Reasonable accommodations not mandatory
sections.summary: SkillsFuture SG works with the Enabling Academy and disability organisations to help training providers offer reasonable accommodations, but implementation is not mandatory.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Hua Han (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While I understand that SkillsFuture SG works with the Enabling Academy and disability organisations, such as DPA, to help training providers offer reasonable accommodations, implementation is not mandatory.

sections.label: Assurance Package cost-of-living support
sections.summary: The Government enhanced the Assurance Package by $1.9 billion, with cash, GST vouchers, U-Save, S&CC rebates and CDC Vouchers to help residents cope with increased costs of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: We had an extensive debate in Parliament in November last year, about the increased costs of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Thus, I am glad that the Government continues to acknowledge the increased costs of living and has enhanced the Assurance Package given to the tune of $1.9 billion so that everyone benefits and those who need more help get a little bit extra.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The disbursement of cash, GST vouchers, U-Save rebates, S&CC rebates and CDC Vouchers will certainly help residents cope with the increased costs of living.

sections.label: Cleaning industry worker shortage
sections.summary: Cleaning companies cannot find cleaners for Town Council conservancy and hawker centre contracts, so the Government is urged to review the foreign worker dependency ratio.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: This shortage of workers can be seen clearly in the cleaning industry where many cleaning companies simply cannot find cleaners, for example for the Town Council conservancy contracts or the cleaning contracts for the hawker centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, I urge the Government to review the foreign worker dependency ratio in areas where we are quite certain that Singaporeans will not want to work.

sections.label: Individual responsibility for skills
sections.summary: The Government's message is that each person is responsible for equipping themselves for the future, with a $4,000 credit for citizens in their 40s or 50s.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But, Sir, the important message from the Government is that each one of us is responsible for equipping ourselves for the future – whether it is for self-improvement or to improve our career prospects, that is for each individual to decide.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: And for citizens in their 40s or 50s, having the $4,000 credit and the opportunity to learn updated skills to enhance their employability is so important.

sections.label: Property tax relief for retirees
sections.summary: A request is made for a review of the owner-occupation property tax hike and a special property tax relief for retirees without income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The Assurance Package has certainly helped them and I want to express my deepest appreciation to the Finance Minister and to the Government for sharing part of Budget 2024 to residents living in private properties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But for those who have no other source of income other than their savings or pension, I wish to make a pitch for them and to ask for a review of the owner-occupation property tax hike.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I appreciate the Government's gesture for adjusting the Annual Value bands for owner occupied residential tax rates.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But for this group of retirees without income, the increase in tax rates last year has caused them distress.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: The 24-month instalment does not help them because it is still the same tax amount payable by these owners which they will have to dig into their savings, nor do they benefit from the other tax measures like the income tax rebate because they do not have any income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: So, Sir, I urge the Government to consider showing appreciation for this small group of retirees without any income by acknowledging their contributions to Singapore and by offering them a special property tax relief.

sections.label: Projected dementia risk increase
sections.summary: By 2030 around 152,000 persons are projected to be at high risk of dementia, and a 2022 American study detailed increased Alzheimer's risk for younger generations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: By 2030, there will be around 152,000 persons projected to be at high risk of dementia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2022, an American study detailed how, Gen X, Y and Z, and even younger generational youths will have a further four-to-six-fold increase in risk of Alzheimer's disease and other forms of dementia.

sections.label: Dementia network at exhibition
sections.summary: On 6 January the Sembawang-Woodlands Dementia Search Activation Network Telegram group was featured at the #DementiaFriendlySG exhibition at the National Museum.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Earlier this year on 6 January, our local ground-up Sembawang-Woodlands Dementia Search Activation Network (D-San) Telegram group was featured at the #DementiaFriendlySG exhibition at the National Museum.

sections.label: Synchronising health and social service boundaries
sections.summary: The issue is disparate methods of deciding service boundaries, and MOH is urged to synchronise regional medical and social services for integrated social-health coordination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The issue is not in having service boundaries, but rather in having disparate and differing methods in deciding service boundaries.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Healthier SG requires a seamless coordination between the medical, social and community services and different approaches may lead to increased friction for professionals and make it more difficult for local ground-up social-health coordination by the various community agencies and medical institutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We must decisively synchronise our regional medical and social services in their service boundary in order to ensure long-term medical-community partnership.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Each town can offer a suite of services across the medical-social spectrum, advancing local medical-social integration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It may be big step forward, but it may also be necessary if we wish to have a seamless integrated social-health system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: These plans will provide Singaporeans with greater access to community senior and mental health services at locales where they live.

sentences.speaker: Ms Poh Li San (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I hope MOH will consider strengthening the resilience and heart-ware of communities and integrating the service boundaries across health and social services.

sections.label: End of post-Cold War era
sections.summary: The three decades of post-Cold War peace and stability are over, and we now live in an era of conflict and confrontation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The three decades of peace and stability in the post-Cold War era is now over, and he shared that we now lived in an era of conflict and confrontation.

sections.label: Competition for quality investments
sections.summary: Competition for quality investments is stiffer, with Japan, Germany and the UAE giving subsidies, so Singapore should strengthen its ecosystem instead of bidding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: However, the competition to attract quality investments is getting stiffer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We have heard of countries, such as Japan, Germany and the United Arab Emirates, rolling out vast amounts of subsidies to attract investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I agree with Deputy Prime Minister Wong that we cannot afford to engage in this "bidding war" with the major economies, but what we can do is to strengthen the vibrant ecosystem that makes it conducive to attract investments in Singapore.

sections.label: MNEs and local SMEs
sections.summary: MNEs including SIA Engineering Company and ST Engineering pursue business development, bringing global jobs to local SMEs and workers through schemes like Partnerships for Capability Transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: MNEs looking to develop their business, including our local homegrown MNEs, like SIA Engineering Company and ST Engineering, pursuing business development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: This then brings in jobs globally for our local small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) who, together with its workers, have a fair share of the pie through schemes, such as the Partnerships for Capability Transformation scheme.

sections.label: Budget 2024 investment measures
sections.summary: Budget 2024 announced $3 billion for RIE 2025 grants, $2 billion top-ups to the National Productivity Fund and Financial Sector Fund, and enhancements to Partnerships for Capability Transformation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We must continue to balance these levers and leverage on more to continue to make Singapore a vibrant and viable investment location.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I am glad that in Budget 2024, it was announced that there are $3 billion investments in the Research, Innovation and Enterprise (RIE) 2025 grants, $2 billion top-ups to the National Productivity Fund (NPF) and Financial Sector Fund each and the enhancements to the Partnerships for Capability Transformation.

sections.label: National AI Strategy 2.0 funding
sections.summary: As a member of the MCI Government Parliamentary Committee, the speaker is glad to see over $1 billion invested over five years for the National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2.0.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As a member of the Ministry of Communications and Information (MCI) Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC), I am also glad to see our commitment to invest in more than $1 billion over five years for our National Artificial Intelligence Strategy 2.0.

sections.label: Refundable Investment Credit tool
sections.summary: The Leader of Opposition quoted Deputy Prime Minister Wong on the darkened international environment, and the speaker says attracting foreign investments is harder and welcomes the Refundable Investment Credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Similar to my speech, the Leader of Opposition quoted Deputy Prime Minister Wong's speech that the "international environment has darkened dramatically" and we expressed caution towards Singapore's future in the uncertain global environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I can tell you for certain that it is getting increasingly difficult to attract foreign investments into Singapore and I am glad that the Refundable Investment Credit is an additional tool introduced to assist in attracting investments into Singapore.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-up welcome
sections.summary: Having raised this in earlier speeches and Bills, the speaker welcomes the enhancements, especially the $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top-up for selected industry-oriented training courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I have raised this in my maiden speech, in the Budget Debate 2022, Income Tax (Amendment) Bill 2023, National Productivity Fund (Amendment) Bill 2023 and SkillsFuture (Amendment) Bill 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome these enhancements, especially the $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top-up, for selected industry-oriented training courses as it will enable our workforce to focus on capability development to drive innovation towards higher value outcomes.

sections.label: Fiscal discipline and social compact
sections.summary: Fiscal discipline, a refreshed social compact and a strong united society will define how Singapore navigates uncertainties and turns challenges into opportunities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: As we head towards the uncertain future our fiscal discipline, our refreshed social compact and our focus on keeping our society strong and united will be integral to define how well we can navigate the uncertainties ahead, turn challenges into opportunities and progress for Singapore and ensure that despite all the challenges ahead of us, we continue to look out for one another, care for one another, in a vibrant, resilient and inclusive community.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chua Kheng Wee Louis (Sengkang)
sentences.text: So, if I am hearing him correctly, is he saying that we should then go against the spirit of BEPS 2.0?

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: I am just saying that when it comes to attracting investments, we should not limit our capability to attracting investments, which would mean requiring us to provide certain benefits or support in order to bring the investments into Singapore.

sections.label: Age discrimination and job vacancies
sections.summary: MOM reports show age was the most common discrimination in job searches, and in the third quarter of 2023 job vacancies still exceeded job seekers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Indeed, according to the Ministry of Manpower's (MOM) Fair Employment Practices Reports, age was the most common form of discrimination encountered during job searches.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the MOM's Labour Market Report for the third quarter of 2023, there were still more job vacancies than job seekers.

sections.label: SEC employers and senior workers
sections.summary: As of September 2022, the SEC was taken up by over 100,000 employers and benefited over 460,000 senior workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As of September 2022, the SEC has been taken up by more than 100,000 employers and benefited more than 460,000 senior workers.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme measures
sections.summary: Budget introduces three SkillsFuture Level-Up measures for Singaporeans aged 40 and above, including a $4,000 credit and diploma subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To assist mid-career workers, this Budget introduces three measures under the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, for Singaporeans aged 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Not having a maximum eligibility age impliedly recognises that a worker remains potentially employable, regardless of age.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I move to the first measure of providing a new $4,000 credit to enrol in courses that are targeted at employability outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If the intention is to assure enrollees of better employability outcomes, will there be any condition attached to participants, such as to secure jobs in certain sectors?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As for the second measure of providing additional subsidies for a full-time diploma study in any area, it was not mentioned that increased employability was a goal of this measure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Would it then be possible to sign up for such subsidised courses simply for enrichment purposes?

sections.label: BEPS Pillar Two and investment credit
sections.summary: BEPS 2.0 Pillar Two sets a 15% minimum effective tax rate for large MNEs, and the Refundable Investment Credit scheme will help affected companies and investors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Pillar Two of BEPS 2.0 introduces a minimum effective tax rate of 15% for large MNEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The introduction of the Refundable Investment Credit scheme will help existing companies and potential investors impacted by the BEPS Pillar 2.

sections.label: EV input tax and SkillsFuture Credit
sections.summary: A question asks whether input tax is claimable on GST for EV-related expenses, and welcomes the SkillsFuture Credit increase from $500 to $4,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: To encourage the early adoption of electric vehicles (EVs), can the input tax be claimable on the GST incurred for expenses related to these EVs?

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I welcome the increase of the SkillsFuture Credit from $500 to $4,000.

sections.label: Assessment time frame and MNC-SME collaboration
sections.summary: A two-to-three-year assessment window can test the measure, and the expanded Partnerships for Capability Transformation scheme aims at deeper MNC-SME collaboration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A limited time frame of two to three years of assessment can be used to ensure the effectiveness of the measure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I also welcome the Government's plan to expand the Partnerships for Capability Transformation scheme, which aims to promote more and deeper collaboration between the multinational corporations (MNCs) and SMEs.

sections.label: Relaxing employment pass and manpower quotas
sections.summary: The speaker hopes for short-term relaxation of the diversity quota in the Complementarity Assessment Framework and flexibility in Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities Scheme quotas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This would help to reduce some of the companies’ expenditure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope that in the short term, the Government can also relax the diversity quota criterion in the Complementarity Assessment Framework for Employment Pass Hires, as firms find it hard to meet the requirement in a tight labour market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: I hope that there can be flexibility in quota adjustment under the Manpower for Strategic Economic Priorities Scheme, which allows eligible firms to hire S Pass and Work Permit holders beyond their existing ceiling for about three years.

sections.label: Increase in WIS payout and income cap
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the rise in WIS payout to $4,900 and the qualifying income cap increase to $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Next, on uplifting lower-wage workers, I welcome the increase in the WIS payout to $4,900 and the increase in the qualifying income cap of $3,000.

sections.label: Indexing WIS and social support to inflation
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government would consider annually indexing WIS and social support schemes to inflation or the consumer price index.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider indexing WIS and social support schemes to inflation or the consumer price index annually?

sections.label: Public education on training grants and courses
sections.summary: Public education campaigns must be conducted so workers know where and how to access training grants and courses through trustworthy channels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Public education campaigns must be conducted to ensure that these workers know where and how to avail and take advantage of these training grants and courses through trustworthy channels.

sections.label: Social mobility in Budget 2024 debate
sections.summary: The speaker raises concern about those left behind and social mobility, seeking greater awareness of the topic in the 2024 Budget debate.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: A deep concern I have is the impact on those left behind as Singapore attempts to surge ahead and maintain its pace in the world today and, in tandem with this concern, is the profound issue of social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: My contribution to this Budget debate seeks to raise greater awareness on the topic of social mobility, its importance and value to us as a people and as a country in the context of our Budget in 2024.

sections.label: Social mobility as cornerstone
sections.summary: Social mobility is described as the cornerstone of a fair and just society.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: Truly, social mobility is, indeed, the cornerstone of a fair and just society.

sections.label: Commitment to Singaporeans
sections.summary: Society must continue to commit to giving its best to get this right for all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: As a society though, we must continue to commit to giving our best to get this right for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-up questions
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit Top-up and renewed access to subsidised full-time diplomas, and asks about the $4,000 amount, the age of 40 and the diploma limit.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: It gives support to our workers to take that step towards learning again.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: And both the $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit Top-up and the opportunity to have a renewed access to subsidised full-time diplomas are very much welcoming news to me.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: I wonder if the Ministry could share what the thought process behind this was, in terms of how the $4,000 top-up amount was arrived at and why not more, the choice of 40 years old as the age to introduce this programme and why it is limited to a diploma programme only.

sections.label: ITE Progression Award
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the ITE Progression Award, which gives qualifying ITE students a further $10,000 CPF top-up in the Ordinary Account upon completing a diploma.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: I am also heartened by the ITE Progression Award.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: It is a welcome nudge for ITE students who qualify to continue on to pursue a diploma and that upon completion of the said diploma, to get a further $10,000 CPF top-up in the Ordinary Account.

sections.label: Monitoring ITE diploma progression
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Ministry monitors the trend, considers a greater quantum if beneficial, and asks whether it could be retrospectively introduced to former ITE students.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: I hope that the Ministry monitors this trend to see how it encourages more ITE graduates to pursue diplomas and, if proven beneficial and well-received, to consider a greater quantum for them in time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: I wonder if the Ministry could confirm whether this could be retrospectively introduced to former ITE students already currently in polytechnics or those who have recently graduated this year.

sections.label: Volunteering scholarship interview story
sections.summary: The speaker recalls interviewing a young woman from a single parent household who had near-perfect polytechnic GPA but was unaware of her study options and lacked role models.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: In my volunteering capacity, I remember interviewing for a scholarship, a young lady from a single parent household, formerly from a neighbourhood secondary school, having done part-time work to support her family, but yet also scoring a near-perfect grade point average (GPA) for her polytechnic studies.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: What struck me and my fellow panellists most about our interview with her was how unaware she was, notwithstanding her sterling grades, about her potential options to study, flourish, to be exceptional and to take on the world.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: Her intellect, humility, real-world resilience and results notwithstanding, she had a lack of role models, was oblivious to the plethora of global options at her feet and how, with the right support, in good time, she could pave the way for her family to a better life, potentially lifting not only herself but also her mother and siblings out of their current life circumstances.

sections.label: Overseas Humanitarian Assistance Tax Deduction Scheme
sections.summary: The Overseas Humanitarian Assistance Tax Deduction Scheme is a reminder of Singaporeans' privilege and means to support people in crisis.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: In light of that, the Overseas Humanitarian Assistance Tax Deduction Scheme (OHAS) is also a welcome reminder of our privilege as a Singaporean society, and the depth of means to which Singaporeans have, relative to others around the world, to provide and support people in crisis to rebuild their lives again.

sections.label: Hope for Budget delivery
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the coming year's Budget further erodes inequalities and allows social mobility to take root, and supports the Budget Statement.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: With that, Mr Speaker, it is my hope that the delivery of this Budget in the coming year continues to further erode inequalities and lends opportunity for social mobility to continue taking root in our midst.

sentences.speaker: Dr Syed Harun Alhabsyi (Nominated Member):
sentences.text: I rise in support of the Budget Statement.

sections.label: Fourth Industrial Revolution job estimates
sections.summary: In the UK, over 20 years, seven million existing jobs could be affected by AI, but 7.2 million jobs could be created.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The current fourth Industrial Revolution is no different.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: It was estimated that in the United Kingdom (UK), over 20 years, seven million existing jobs could be affected by AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But very critically, 7.2 million jobs could be created.

sections.label: PDPC modelled AI governance framework
sections.summary: In 2019, the Personal Data Protection Commission first realised the modelled AI governance framework.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: For instance, in 2019, the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) first realised the modelled AI governance framework.

sections.label: Singapore AI governance initiatives
sections.summary: Since 2022 Singapore launched AI Verify and an AI Governance Testing framework and toolkit, and in January 2024 a modelled AI governance framework for GenAI systems.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Since 2022, Singapore has also launched initiatives, such as AI Verify and AI Governance Testing framework and toolkit, one of the world's first, and in January 2024, a new modelled AI governance framework for GenAI systems.

sections.label: US, EU and China AI rules
sections.summary: The US has an AI Bill of Rights blueprint, the EU's AI Act adopts a risk-based approach, and China adopted outcomes-based regulations including GenAI measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The United States (US) has a blueprint for an AI Bill of Rights for responsible design and use of AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the European Union (EU), the AI Act, which recently received political endorsement, adopts a risk-based approach to regulating AI applications and rules surrounding transparency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: China has adopted outcomes-based regulations, including interim measures for the management of GenAI services and the Internet information service algorithmic recommendation management provisions.

sections.label: Mid-career reskilling support measures
sections.summary: The Government provides $4,000 SkillsFuture credits for mid-career top-ups and up to $3,000 monthly training allowance for selected full-time courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And here, I would also like to invite the Member to take a look at what the Government is doing to have mid-career reskilling.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We are providing $4,000 in SkillsFuture credits for mid-career top-ups in May 2024, which can be used for selected industry-oriented training courses with better employability outcomes, and up to $3,000 monthly SkillsFuture mid-career training allowance for up to 24 months for selected full-time courses.

sections.label: Policies changing residents' lives
sections.summary: The House is called to make policies and statistics that change residents' lives, and the Government is pushing out policies, initiatives and fiscal provision.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But that is what we are called to do in this House; to make the policies and the statistics and change the lives of our residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: And when Ramasamy came in with his certificate from SIT, the family said and shared with me, "Now, I think it is time for us to buy our flat." That was a very moving sharing with the family.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: So, I could not agree more with Ms Sylvia Lim's point that we cannot forget our seniors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: But where I diverge humbly and respectfully is that we are doing that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We are pushing out policies, we are pushing out initiatives and we are pushing out a lot of fiscal provision.

sections.label: Ageism in the workplace
sections.summary: The speech focuses on older workers and tackling workplace ageism, with MOM reports showing age discrimination is the main form of discrimination.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The main focus of my speech really is on older workers and how we need to tackle ageism in workplace and the Government's own statistics, MOM's own Fair Employment Practices reports, highlight that age discrimination is the main form of discrimination that needs to be tackled.

sections.label: Measures working in concert
sections.summary: Fiscal measures and on-the-ground job matching work together to help residents get as close to a job as they want.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: Not to throw the baby out with the bathwater.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: These are a slew of measures that work in concert with each other – the fiscal measures as well as what we do on the ground for residents to job match and to ensure that they get as close to a job as they want, not only for their own sake but for the sake of their residents.

sections.label: Bridging fiscal policy and families
sections.summary: MPs bridge the gap by translating fiscal policies into real-life examples, and the speaker hopes anti-discrimination legislation will be a game changer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: I do not agree that it is unassailable.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: And the formula for that, the remedy or the solution for that is what the MPs do on the ground to bridge that gap, to translate fiscal policies and all that Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong had said in his Budget 2024 speech into real-life examples of how this has worked and impacted families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza
sentences.text: But the winning formula really is, as backbenchers, our calling and our vocation, to bridge that gap.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I never said that ageism is unassailable and, in fact, in my speech, I expressed the hope that the upcoming anti-discrimination legislation would move the needle and be a game changer.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I hope that your patience will pay off in that you will enjoy your lunch when you are much hungrier.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: I rise in support of the Budget, which lays out a confident path forward for Singapore, as our domestic and global environments change.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The global economy goes through cycles and we are currently facing a slow growth, high inflation environment.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This year’s Budget, including the Enterprise Support Package and enhanced Assurance Package, is comprehensive and includes good support for companies and households to tackle immediate challenges.

sections.label: Economic growth in the 2010s
sections.summary: The economy grew 5% in the 2010s even as labour force growth slowed to 2.1% per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our economy managed to chalk up growth of 5% in the 2010s, even as labour force growth slowed to 2.1% per annum.

sections.label: Structural policies for productivity growth
sections.summary: The passage states that structural policies are needed to drive productivity-driven growth and that restructuring must be undertaken and intensified along three prongs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: To continue growing the economy, we need structural policies to drive productivity-driven growth and take Singapore forward.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We must continue to undertake and intensify our restructuring along three prongs.

sections.label: SkillsFuture participation increase
sections.summary: Annual participation in SkillsFuture initiatives rose from 380,000 people in 2016 to 560,000 people in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our overall annual participation in SkillsFuture initiatives has increased from 380,000 people in 2016 to 560,000 people in 2022.

sections.label: Economic and productivity growth rates
sections.summary: From 2016 to 2023, real value-added growth was 2.8% per annum and productivity growth was 1.7% per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Between 2016 and 2023, our economy achieved real value-added growth of 2.8% per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: In the same period, our productivity growth, in terms of real value-add per worker, was 1.7% per annum.

sections.label: Median income growth of residents
sections.summary: The median income of full-time residents grew at 1.5% per annum in real terms from 2016 to 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The median income of full-time residents grew at 1.5% per annum in real terms from 2016 to 2023.

sections.label: SkillsFuture credits and Level-Up programme
sections.summary: 192,000 Singaporeans used SkillsFuture credits in 2022, and mid-career Singaporeans can use the new SkillsFuture Level-Up programme.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Some 192,000 Singaporeans utilised their SkillsFuture credits in 2022 for self-initiated learning.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Going forward, mid-career Singaporeans can use the new SkillsFuture Level-Up programme, with advisory and support from our agencies, unions and industry, to further their knowledge, skills and careers.

sections.label: RIE funding and innovation ranking
sections.summary: The passage states an additional S$3 billion injection to the 2025 RIE plan and notes Singapore's fifth rank in the 2023 Global Innovation Index.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: As such, the additional S$3 billion injection to our 2025 RIE plan, announced at Budget by Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, is a timely one, as we seek to deepen capabilities in new growth areas like AI, sustainability and advanced manufacturing.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Singapore is ranked fifth in the 2023 Global Innovation Index, and the top in Asia.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Total business expenditure on R&D has grown significantly over the past decade, on par with GDP growth.

sections.label: Patsnap customers and countries
sections.summary: Patsnap has more than 12,000 customers in over 50 countries.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Today, Patsnap has more than 12,000 customers in over 50 countries.

sections.label: Amperesand seed funding
sections.summary: Amperesand, the first deep tech startup under this partnership, raised over US$12 million in seed funding to scale its solid-state transformer technology.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Amperesand, the first deep tech startup supported under this partnership, has already raised over US$12 million in seed funding to scale up its solid-state transformer technology for the fast charging of electric vehicles.

sections.label: Enterprise Innovation Scheme tax deductions
sections.summary: The Enterprise Innovation Scheme provides tax deduction and allowances on qualifying expenditures including R&D, IP registration, IP rights acquisition, training and innovation projects with IHLs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The Enterprise Innovation Scheme provides tax deduction and allowances on qualifying expenditures like R&D, intellectual property (IP) registration, IP rights acquisition, training and innovation projects with our IHLs.

sections.label: Singapore agreements and global nodes
sections.summary: Singapore has 27 FTAs, 42 International Investment Agreements, around 100 avoidance of double taxation agreements, four Digital Economy Agreements and 21 nodes across Asia Pacific, Europe and the US.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have built up strong connections to the region and the world through our extensive set of agreements.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We have 27 Free Trade Agreements (FTAs) in force, 42 International Investment Agreements and around 100 avoidance of double taxation agreements, and we have since innovated and evolved new forms of cooperation, such as the four Digital Economy Agreements.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Our 21 nodes across Asia Pacific, Europe and the US facilitate Singapore-based enterprises to explore new markets and reap synergies.

sections.label: 2023 commitments jobs and value-added
sections.summary: The 2023 commitments are expected to create over 20,000 jobs with a projected $26.7 billion in value-added per annum, and Singapore hosts some 37,000 international companies and 7,000 MNEs.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The 2023 commitments are expected to create over 20,000 jobs, with a projected contribution of $26.7 billion in value-added per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: And this is why Singapore is home to some 37,000 international companies and 7,000 MNEs, many of which use Singapore as their regional headquarters.

sections.label: Transformation, skills upgrading, international cooperation
sections.summary: Business leaders and employees are aware of transformation and skills upgrading and act proactively, and Singapore must strengthen international connection and cooperation to consolidate its position as a Global-Asia node.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: What heartens me is that our business leaders and employees are aware of the importance of transformation and skills upgrading, and act proactively.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: This will allow us to consolidate our momentum in key economic sectors and enhance the competitiveness of local enterprises.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: Thirdly, we must strengthen international connection and cooperation to consolidate Singapore's position as a Global-Asia node for technology, innovation and enterprise.

sections.label: Singapore as trusted connector node
sections.summary: Singapore can create value by facilitating connections and offering an innovation ecosystem as a base for new ventures.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: By serving as a trusted node and connector, we can create value by facilitating connections and building new linkages in today's fractured global landscape.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: We can offer a strong innovation ecosystem with leading capabilities, talent and companies, making Singapore an ideal base to grow and build new ventures.

sections.label: AI, reskilling and SkillsFuture credits
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister said AI can be augmented intelligence and workers need reskilling, and asked whether SkillsFuture credits should be expanded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Deputy Prime Minister said that AI can be our augmented intelligence and that we should think hard about how jobs will be changed with automation and AI, and he said that we need to reskill our workers to prepare for AI.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, given that seven in 10 people have not used their SkillsFuture credits since the scheme was started in 2015, does Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat think that it will be useful to expand the use of the SkillsFuture credits beyond core subsidies and give all students and workers more opportunities for hands-on practice with deep tech tools, like AI?

sections.label: Low SkillsFuture take-up and older workers
sections.summary: Take-up of SkillsFuture credits remains low, especially among older workers, and the question asks how the Government will raise it.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Yet, as my hon friend has shared, statistics reveal that, in recent times, take-up remains low.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: And in fact, many have yet to exhaust their SkillsFuture credits, even as the Government has proposed that we increase them.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: But perhaps, what is even more damning is that older workers, exactly the group that we hope will take on this task of reskilling, display significantly lower take-up rates.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: My question is, in light of the wrenching changes that AI will usher in, how would the Government ensure that SkillsFuture will actually be able to increase its take-up rate and fulfil the objective of reskilling that it was meant to accomplish or is it revealing that there is a continued scepticism among our workers of the benefits of the scheme?

sections.label: SkillsFuture credit usage rate
sections.summary: Only three in 10 have used their SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: Only three in 10 have used their SkillsFuture credits.

sections.label: Take-up not sole learning indicator
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Credit take-up or adoption rate must not be seen as the only indicator of learning.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Credit take-up or adoption rate must not be seen as the only indicator of learning.

sections.label: Credits and free programmes
sections.summary: More SkillsFuture credits can be used, but that must not be the only indicator because many free programmes did not require the credits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: While we know that we can use more of the SkillsFuture credits, that must not be the only indicator, because there are lots of free programmes that did not require the use of these credits.

sections.label: Attitude towards lifelong learning
sections.summary: It is about an attitude towards learning and inculcating interest and passion to learn throughout life, not take-up rates or courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In short, it is really about an attitude towards learning, that we must inculcate this interest and passion to learn, and learn throughout your lives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: It is not about the take-up rate and not about the courses, it is not about putting up more of these.

sections.label: Household income data
sections.summary: A 12 February 2024 report showed lowest-earning households' real incomes dropped 1.7% in 2022 while median household income rose 2.8%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Today, I will speak with that light in mind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was reported on 12 February 2024 that the lowest-earning households in Singapore saw their real incomes dropped by 1.7% in 2022, after accounting for inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The same report, the data from the Department of Statistics, showed the median household income for the same period rose by 2.8%.

sections.label: Maximum housing purchase amount
sections.summary: Assuming a 50/50 split per section, the maximum amount a household receives for purchasing their own home is $15,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If you assume a 50/50 split in the amounts the household received for each section, the maximum amount of household receives for purchasing their own home is $15,000.

sections.label: Insufficient downpayment support
sections.summary: Even after accounting for the household contribution, the total level of support would be insufficient for the downpayment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Even after accounting for the household contribution, the total level of support would be insufficient for the downpayment.

sections.label: Naturalising foreign spouses
sections.summary: Singaporeans whose spouses failed to get PR or LTVP are deprived of matrimonial life, so a path towards naturalising foreign spouses including housing policies is needed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Singaporeans whom I met in this situation have been unsuccessful in applying for their spouse to obtain PR status or even a Long-Term Visit Pass (LTVP).

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They are effectively deprived of having a matrimonial life with their spouses in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some of them also rely on their spouse to be their caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: We need to consider streamlining a path towards naturalising foreign spouses in Singapore, which includes housing policies for such families.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With clear key performance indicators, such as improved per capita household income benchmarked against the median, we can better track how well policies are working and do the necessary fine-tuning.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Credit Scheme reimbursements
sections.summary: The enhancement of the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme is a step in the right direction, and the Government could consider shortening reimbursement periods to aid enterprises' cashflows.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The enhancement of the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme is a step in the right direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to ask if the Government can consider shortening the period for reimbursements to aid enterprises' cashflows.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme credit
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme offers an additional $4,000 credit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme offers an additional $4,000 credit.

sections.label: Employer feedback on curriculum relevance
sections.summary: It asks what structure ensures a swift employer feedback loop on curriculum relevance and what procedures ensure timely adaptation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: What is the structure in place to ensure a swift feedback loop from employers on the relevance of curriculum and what are the procedures to ensure timely adaption?

sections.label: Adult learners long-form diploma allowance
sections.summary: Adult learners can take time off for a long-form diploma with a monthly allowance of up to $3,000 for 24 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Adult learners can take time off to pursue a long-form diploma with a provision of a monthly allowance of up to $3,000 for 24 months.

sections.label: Employee Stock Ownership Plans adoption
sections.summary: One promising avenue is the more widespread adoption of Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs).

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: One promising avenue is the more widespread adoption of Employee Stock Ownership Plans (ESOPs).

sections.label: Netherlands stock options tax point
sections.summary: In the Netherlands, the tax point for stock options has shifted to when shares become tradable, rather than at exercise or alienation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: In the Netherlands, the tax point for stock options has been shifted to a more favourable time for employees, that is, when the shares become tradable, rather than at the moment of exercise or alienation.

sections.label: Singapore share-based remuneration tax incentives
sections.summary: Comparing these models to Singapore's tax incentives, there may be room to expand incentives for a broader range of alternatives to ESOPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Comparing these models to Singapore's current tax incentives; while Singapore has a framework to support share-based remuneration, there may be room to expand these incentives to encourage a broader range of alternatives to ESOPs.

sections.label: Blended capital deployment programmes
sections.summary: Suggests Enterprise Singapore and NVPC collaborate on programmes to expand deployment of blended capital.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To augment this trend, I suggest that agencies, such as Enterprise Singapore and National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre (NVPC), collaborate to devise programmes aimed at expanding the deployment of blended capital.

sections.label: Enabling Masterplan 2030 strategic themes
sections.summary: EMP2030 identified three strategic themes: lifelong learning support, independent living, and inclusive physical and social environments.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To enable PwDs to flourish, our national roadmap for disability inclusion, the Enabling Masterplan 2030 (EMP2030), identified three strategic themes: one, to strengthen support for lifelong learning; two, to enable independent living; and three, to create inclusive physical and social environments for persons of all abilities.

sections.label: Enabling Services and Business Hubs
sections.summary: The first Enabling Services Hub in Tampines West Community Club and Enabling Business Hub in Jurong launched last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The first Enabling Services Hub (ESH) in the Tampines West Community Club and the Enabling Business Hub (EBH) in Jurong launched last year, were a few examples.

sections.label: Disability data sharing and consultation scheduling
sections.summary: Better disability data capture and cross-sector sharing would help professionals plan, and fixed consultation rhythms may reduce wait time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Better capture of disability data and sharing across sectors, including social services, healthcare and transport, would enable professionals to plan and do better for PwDs that they serve, according to their unique circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: A fixed rhythm of consultation sessions may be planned for patients that are used to certain set routines, for instance, seeing a doctor only in the mornings or scheduling patients only at the start or the end of a shift to significantly reduce wait time.

sections.label: Medication for behavioural outbursts
sections.summary: For some PwDs, medication is sometimes prescribed to help manage behavioural outbursts.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For some PwDs, medication is sometimes prescribed to help them manage behavioural outbursts.

sections.label: Cross-sector support for PwDs and caregivers
sections.summary: Healthcare and social work professionals reinforcing messages, referring to SNTC, and clarifying policies like CareShield Life would benefit PwDs and caregivers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: For instance, having healthcare professionals take a more 360° view of the patients and caregivers they serve, by reinforcing messages, such as the importance of future care planning where opportune or, even better, refer them to organisations like the Special Needs Trust Company (SNTC).

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: In other instances, having social work professionals help clear up doubts that PwDs and their caregivers might have about policies, such as CareShield Life, would only benefit the very individuals and families that these professionals from the different sectors are all trying to serve.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Information such as unique circumstances that might trigger a meltdown, habits or routines unique to each person, the loss of such information along the way, among others, that affords each organisation working with the PwDs and their caregivers a better chance of providing a more person-centric service has to be minimised.

sections.label: Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme Voucher
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the Budget announcement of a one-year PPHS (Open Market) Voucher to help eligible families rent an HDB flat in the open market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: But family circumstances change and with the welcoming of another baby or two, the living conditions in the flat will be too cramped.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Hence, I welcome Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong’s announcement in this year’s Budget of the new Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS) (Open Market) Voucher for one year, to support eligible families to rent an HDB flat in the open market.

sections.label: Longer voucher rental period
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the open market rental vouchers can be provided for two years, since HDB's average BTO waiting time is three to four years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The PPHS (Open Market) Voucher will be useful for families like Mdm Nur to have interim housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: However, since according to HDB, the average waiting time for BTOs is between three to four years, I hope that such vouchers for rental flats in the open market can be provided for a period of two years, so that such young couples with children can enter into a longer tenancy period.

sections.label: Project Dian@M3 locations
sections.summary: Project Dian@M3 is rolled out in six areas and now supports more than 400 families in rental flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Project Dian@M3 is rolled out in Bedok, Geylang Serai, Jalan Besar, Jurong, Chua Chu Kang and Tampines, and now supports more than 400 families in rental flats.

sections.label: Blocks without direct lift access
sections.summary: About 150 blocks in Singapore still lack direct lift access after the LUP, with 20% of them in Keat Hong.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Even after HDB’s Lift Upgrading Programme (LUP), there are still about 150 blocks remaining in Singapore that do not have direct lift access.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Out of these 150 segmented blocks, 20% of them in Singapore are found in Keat Hong, which means these families do not have same-floor lift access.

sections.label: Keat Hong segmented flats survey
sections.summary: A survey found almost two in three segmented unit flats in Keat Hong have an elderly person or child, and 28 LHG applications were approved as at December 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Based on my survey during house visits, almost two in three segmented unit flats in Keat Hong have either an elderly person or a child living there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In an answer to my Parliamentary Question, there were 28 approved applications as at December 2021 for LHG out of an estimated 2,000 affected HDB units that have no lift access.

sections.label: LUP cost sharing approach
sections.summary: The speaker says the approach would raise benefiting dwelling units in Keat Hong from 12% to 15% to more than 50%, sharing costs within the LUP cost cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: By including such an approach, the dwelling units for each block that will benefit from LUP, using the examples in Keat Hong, would improve from a mere 12% to 15%, to more than 50% of the entire block.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: This means that the costs can be shared among more households to come within the LUP cost cap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: During the Selective Renewal Lift Programmes in Keat Hong, many non-segmented unit households experienced for themselves firsthand how it was like to live in a segmented unit when their serving lifts were temporarily shut down for renewal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The residents told me that they now empathise and would support a different approach towards LUP costing.

sections.label: Visiting blocks in constituency
sections.summary: The speaker says visiting such blocks in his constituency requires more patience, time and energy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Mr Zhulkarnain, I have a few of those blocks in my constituency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: When I do visits to those blocks, you need more patience, you need to cater more time and you expend more energy.

sections.label: Budget estimates lack breakdown
sections.summary: Military expenditure is a single $19 billion line making up 17% of the Budget, and Police projects Arapaima and Aegis get hundreds of millions without public description.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The yearly revenue and expenditure estimates are a good place to start.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: This year, military expenditure is a single line $19 billion expenditure without further breakdown, despite making up 17% of the Budget.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Likewise, in the case of the Police expenditures contained in the estimates, where projects named "Arapaima" and "Aegis" are allocated hundreds of millions of dollars each but the public are not provided even with a one-line description.

sections.label: Singapore Gini coefficient differences
sections.summary: Singapore's Gini coefficient may differ because it cites work income, excludes non-work income growth, and covers only Citizens and PRs, not the 1.5 million foreign workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Perhaps, it is because Singapore's Gini coefficient cites income from work while OECD countries count income from all sources, and commentators have also pointed out that household expenditure survey data has shown that income from non-work sources has been increasing in Singapore or, perhaps, it is because Singapore's Gini coefficient covers only Citizens and Permanent Residents (PRs), unlike other countries, and does not reflect that much of our essential but lower-paid blue-collar work, which is performed by our total foreign workforce of 1.5 million individuals.

sections.label: Singapore wealth inequality ranking
sections.summary: The UBS Global Wealth Report indicates Singapore's 2022 wealth inequality is 78.8, higher than Taiwan's 69.8, Korea's 67.9 and Japan's 65.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: The UBS' Global Wealth Report indicates that Singapore's wealth inequality in 2022 is 78.8, substantially higher than Taiwan's 69.8, Korea's 67.9 and Japan's 65.

sections.label: Ireland citizens assembly example
sections.summary: In Ireland, parliament directors established a 2016 citizens' assembly of 99 demographically representative citizens, with experts providing testimony and case studies.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: A well-known example of this is in Ireland, where the Irish parliament directors established a citizens' assembly in 2016 to deliberate several socially contentious issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Ninety-nine citizens, demographically suited to representing Ireland's electorate, were chosen to deliberate the issues, with experts also brought into the forum to provide testimony and discuss case studies.

sections.label: Dashboard beyond GDP call
sections.summary: The speaker reiterates a call for Singapore to have a dashboard measuring well-being beyond GDP, with policies considering their impact on these indicators.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: We must regularly quantify, measure and publish details on how we are doing and to ask that our policies formally consider the impact that they are having on these indicators, and whether or not our various policies and initiatives are successful in improving our collective well-being.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: I would therefore like to reiterate the call I made two years ago, for Singapore to have a dashboard with measurements of how we are doing beyond GDP measurements.

sections.label: Singapore dashboard key areas
sections.summary: The speaker says a Singapore dashboard should cover unpaid work, natural resource use, environmental footprint, leisure value and well-being, subject to public input.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: While the specific details of what should be included in Singapore's dashboard would be subject to input from public bodies and the wider community, I believe the key areas that should be covered include the measurement of unpaid work, natural resource use, specifically, our people, externality cost in a form of environmental sustainability footprint, leisure value and our collective and individual well-being.

sections.label: Caregiving costs and carer support
sections.summary: A Duke-NUS team estimated $2.5 to $3.5 billion annual informal caregiving cost for seniors 75 and above, and Forward Singapore lists carer support measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Although, in 2021, the Duke-NUS team estimated an annual cost of caregiving time of between $2.5 to $3.5 billion in informal care being provided for seniors aged 75 and above who need human assistance of daily activities.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Additionally, the Forward Singapore report also lists a variety of ways and means which policy can better support informal carers, such as enhancing parental and infant care leave, allowing more flexible work arrangements, and also financial support in the form of the Home Caregiving Grant and defraying early intervention costs for families with special needs children.

sections.label: SkillsFuture utilisation and inclusiveness
sections.summary: The speaker hopes SkillsFuture becomes more attractive and inclusive, noting utilisation rates of around 50% in 2022 show more work is needed.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Additionally, I hope that the SkillsFuture framework continues to work towards being more attractive and inclusive for Singaporeans across a broad spectrum.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: It is clearly an area which needs more work, as can be seen by utilisation rates of around 50% in 2022.

sections.label: Paid learning leave calls
sections.summary: Calls by NTUC for paid learning leave can partly address structural impediments to workers taking up useful training programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Calls, such as those made by NTUC, for paid learning leave can go some way to addressing these structural impediments to workers taking up useful training programmes.

sections.label: Enterprise Support Package and loans
sections.summary: The $1.3 billion Enterprise Support Package helps companies with challenges and capabilities, and the EFS-SME loan maximum rises to $500,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The $1.3 billion Enterprise Support Package will go a long way to help companies tide over current challenges and build long-term capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The increase in the maximum loan quantum under the EFS-SME Working Capital Loan to $500,000 will help them meet higher capital and cashflow requirements in an environment of rising costs.

sections.label: Ringfencing RIE2025 and AI funds
sections.summary: The speaker suggests ringfencing a portion of the additional $3 billion for RIE2025 and over $1 billion AI investment for SMEs or SME collaborations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Regarding the additional $3 billion commitment to the $25 billion RIE2025 plan and over $1 billion investment in the next five years into AI compute, talent and industry development, may I suggest that a portion of both be ringfenced for SMEs or collaborations involving SMEs?

sections.label: Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund progress
sections.summary: The passage asks for an update on the $60 million Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund, whether the target is on track, how much has been disbursed, and what projects it supports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Would the Government provide an update on the progress of $60 million Agri-Food Cluster Transformation Fund?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Are we on track to meet this target?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How much of the fund has been disbursed and what kind of projects does it support?

sections.label: Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements
sections.summary: The Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests are expected later this year and could include examples of reasonable and unreasonable business grounds, with most of the public sector working up to two days a week from home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangement Requests (TG-FWAR) are expected to be released later this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The guidelines could include examples of reasonable and unreasonable business grounds to justify why requested FWAs can or cannot be provided.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I understand that for most of the public sector, working up to two days a week from home is the norm.

sections.label: Correction on SkillsFuture training rates
sections.summary: The speaker corrects an earlier mention of utilisation rates of around 50% in 2022, clarifying that they meant training rates of around 50% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: Earlier on, in my speech on the SkillsFuture framework, I mentioned utilisation rates of around 50% in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
sentences.text: What I meant was training rates of around 50% in 2022.

sections.label: BEPS 2.0 and Refundable Investment Credit
sections.summary: Singapore's participation in the OECD-led BEPS 2.0 framework provides a tailor-made channel for creating incentives for AI adoption, and DPM Lawrence Wong's proposed Refundable Investment Credit appears aligned with qualified refundable tax credits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Singapore's participation in the OECD-led BEPS 2.0 framework affords us a tailor-made channel for creating incentives for AI adoption across a whole range of firm types.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's proposed Refundable Investment Credit appears aligned with such qualified refundable tax credits.

sections.label: BEPS top-up tax and credit perception
sections.summary: BEPS rules permit countries to independently apply a top-up tax if they believe tax rates on firms domiciled in Singapore circumvent the 15% minimum or subvert the credit's intent, especially if the Refundable Investment Credit is perceived as a loophole.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Second, while there is room for defining the scope of such credits, it is important to be mindful that BEPS rules permit countries to independently apply a top-up tax, which they may do if they believe that the tax rates imposed on firms domiciled here circumvents the spirit of the 15% minimum or subverts the intent of the credit to encourage sustainability or knowledge generation, in particular, if the Refundable Investment Credit is perceived as an instrument designed as a loophole.

sections.label: Generative AI productivity gains
sections.summary: Emerging evidence suggests generative AI boosts productivity by about 14%, with gains of around 34% among novice and low-skilled workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
