sentences.text: Emerging evidence suggests that generative AI boosts productivity by about 14%.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: But among novice and low-skilled workers, the gain was far more, something to the order of 34%.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit expansion
sections.summary: The speaker argues SkillsFuture Credit's scale should be ramped up and its scope expanded, valuing knowledge beyond the classroom.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: It is imperative, therefore, that we do not devalue alternative forms of knowledge acquisition beyond the classroom.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: That is why I believe that not only should the scale of SkillsFuture Credit be ramped up, as Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong indicated in the Level-Up Programme, but its scope should be expanded.

sections.label: Apprenticeship programmes using SkillsFuture credits
sections.summary: The speaker hopes companies with credible apprenticeship proposals can take on trainees who apply with their SkillsFuture credits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: I wish to elaborate on the idea here but take it a step further.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: I hope that we can consider allowing companies that are able to submit credible proposals for apprenticeship programmes to take on trainees that apply with their SkillsFuture credits.

sections.label: Support for involuntarily unemployed workers
sections.summary: The speaker says Lawrence Wong's indication of temporary financial support for the involuntarily unemployed, including the redundant, is important.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Inevitably, some workers will be displaced by AI.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: This is why Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong's indication that there will be temporary financial support for the involuntarily unemployed, in other words, support for those that have been made redundant is important.

sections.label: Reconsidering high stakes standardised tests
sections.summary: The speaker says high stakes standardised tests as a performance benchmark need reconsidering since AI outperforms humans in many exams.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: First, we need to reconsider the importance of high stakes standardised tests as a performance benchmark, since AI already outperforms humans in most exams or they will in the next few years, in areas ranging from accounting, to law, to medicine, to languages.

sections.label: Banning students from using AI
sections.summary: The speaker says banning students from AI is wrong and calling ChatGPT output plagiarism disadvantages them in the real world.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The tempting, but wrong, solution is to ban our students from using AI altogether.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: We do our students a disservice when we insist carte blanche that using ChatGPT output constitutes plagiarism, because this would disadvantage them when they enter into the real world and are forced to compete with those with greater familiarity of how to integrate generative AI into their work.

sections.label: Continuous assessment and Edusave top-up
sections.summary: The speaker says continuous assessment needs to be taken more seriously and Wong's Edusave Endowment Fund top-up could realign mindsets on competencies beyond grades.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Continuous assessment, a term that we have used to describe our model of evaluation since I was in primary school, needs to be taken far more seriously.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: And Deputy Prime Minister Wong's decision to top up the Edusave Endowment Fund has the potential to contribute to realigning our mindsets on competencies beyond grades.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: But I would encourage the MOE to take bolder steps, such as increasing the number of non-academic awards, making final exams just a small fraction of the overall course grade and allowing through-train education without the Primary School Leaving Examination (PSLE).

sections.label: ITE Progression Award and AI
sections.summary: DPM Wong's ITE Progression Award, which gives ITE graduates financial support for diploma programmes, should be viewed in light of what AI means for credentialism.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong's announcement of the ITE Progression Award, an effort to provide additional financial support to ITE graduates seeking to enrol in diploma programmes, should thus be viewed in light of what AI means for credentialism.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: While upgrading skills is undeniably important, promoting the acquisition of yet another paper qualification may be an incomplete assessment of the upgrader's abilities or, even worse, proffer a misguided reassurance that doing so will necessarily translate into a job and hence, be disappointed.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: The last thing we want from a 21st century government and legislature is more canned answers and pro-forma solutions that look like they came out of ChatGPT.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim
sentences.text: More crucially, we need the courage and conviction to forge a new way forward that is unshackled from our old ways.

sections.label: Enterprise Support Package for SMEs
sections.summary: The $1.3 billion Enterprise Support Package includes a 50% corporate income tax rebate capped at $40,000 and a minimum cash benefit of $2,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The $1.3 billion Enterprise Support Package, which includes a 50% corporate income tax rebate capped at $40,000 and a minimum cash benefit of $2,000, will be particularly advantageous for our SMEs.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme
sections.summary: The SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme for Singaporeans aged 40 and above includes a $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top-up, the Mid-Career Enhancement Subsidy and a monthly training allowance of up to $3,000 for up to 24 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Introducing the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme for Singaporeans aged 40 and above is a commendable step.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Including the $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top-up that fills the need for lifelong learning, even in times of inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This initiative, coupled with the Mid-Career Enhancement Subsidy and a monthly training allowance of up to $3,000 for up to 24 months will significantly motivate individuals to enhance their skills.

sections.label: Skills, income and minimum cash payout
sections.summary: Empowering individuals with new skills can elevate real income through productivity gains and prepare Singapore for the changing economic climate, and the minimum cash payout of $2,000 benefits many Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Not only will empowering individuals with new and improved skills enable us to elevate real income through productivity gains, this will also allow Singapore to be better prepared for the ever-changing economic climate as well as create an agile and relevant workforce to better solidify our position in the world as more than a financial hub.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also believe the minimum cash payout of $2,000 to all companies which employ at least one local employee is clearly a new feature that will benefit many Singaporeans.

sections.label: Higher ERS from 2025
sections.summary: From 2025 the ERS will be raised to four times the Basic Retirement Sum, allowing a member to receive $3,330 a month from age 65 for life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From 2025, the ERS – the maximum that can be put in the RA – will be raised to four times the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS).

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With the higher ERS, a member can receive $3,330 a month from age 65 for life, against currently $2,530 at the current ERS level.

sections.label: Recommendation to lower FRS
sections.summary: The recommendation is for the FRS to be adjusted down to 1.6 times the BRS from the current 2.0 times, a reduction of $40,600 in the threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In order to make the path to FRS and then eventually ERS less steep, my recommendation is for the FRS to be adjusted down to 1.6 times the level of BRS from the current 2.0 times.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In dollar terms, from the current level of $213,000 to $170,400, a reduction of $40,600 in the threshold.

sections.label: Education subsidies and SkillsFuture Credit
sections.summary: Government subsidises 75% of tuition fees for all Singaporeans and 90% for those aged 40 and above, with a $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top-up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: For part-time and post-diploma programmes, the full fee is typically around $19,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But the Government is already subsidising 90% of such fees for Singaporeans aged 40 and above, or around $17,000, such that the nett fees payable to the Singaporean is less than $2,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And so, the SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $4,000 will more than cover the typical fees after subsidies for part-time and post-diploma programmes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: But for all Singaporeans, the Government is subsidising 75% of tuition fees, or almost $23,000 over 2.5 years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And so, when Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong said in the Budget Statement that the Government is giving every Singaporean aged 40 and above a second "bite of the education subsidy", this bite is, in my mind, worth $23,000.

sections.label: Training allowance for mid-life studies
sections.summary: Government introduces a training allowance tagged to recent income, capped at $3,000 monthly for up to 24 months, totalling up to $72,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Indeed, on top of all these subsidies and credits, the Government is also introducing a training allowance tagged to one's average recent income to reduce the opportunity cost of pursuing full-time studies mid-life.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: This training allowance is capped at $3,000 per month for up to 24 months; so, up to $72,000 in total.

sections.label: Additional cost per citizen
sections.summary: For the Government, this would mean an additional cost of up to $18,000 per citizen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: For the Government, this would mean an additional cost of up to $18,000 per citizen.

sections.label: ITE and diploma graduate pay gap
sections.summary: ITE graduate starting pay is around $8,000 lower yearly than diploma graduate pay, with a CPF Ordinary Account gap of around $1,500 per year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: The starting pay for an ITE graduate is around $8,000 lower than that for a diploma graduate on a full-year basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And so, the gap in CPF Ordinary Account contributions alone is around $1,500 per year.

sections.label: Uplifting ITE and polytechnic wages
sections.summary: Government announced up to $9 billion over five years in Workfare and the Progressive Wage Model to uplift ITE and polytechnic graduate wages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And for our corporates – our enterprises and employers – I hope they will accord ever greater recognition of the skills that both our ITE and polytechnic graduates possess, and join hands with the Government to continue uplifting the wages of both our ITE and polytechnic graduates in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And last year, the Government has announced it will invest up to $9 billion over five years, in both Workfare and the Progressive Wage Model (PWM), to achieve this.

sections.label: Revision in income thresholds
sections.summary: With revised income thresholds, more Singaporeans will keep or regain their blue card at renewal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: I have met so many residents who got "bumped down" to the "orange" card or "green" card because their children are staying with them are earning a bit more than the "blue" card threshold.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And so, with the revision in income thresholds more Singaporeans will get to keep their "blue" card or regain their "blue" card at renewal.

sections.label: GST and national budgets
sections.summary: Taking the easy way out on GST since 1993 would have left Singapore $19 billion poorer, equal to its entire health budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Had we taken the easy way out on GST each time, starting from 1993, we would be $19 billion poorer today, literally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Nineteen billion dollars is our entire health budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: It is our entire Education and early childhood education budgets combined.

sections.label: GST and Net Investment Returns
sections.summary: Without GST increases since 1993, almost all Net Investment Returns would be used instead of just over half.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: — starting from 1993, we would be talking today about using almost all of our Net Investment Returns and not just a bit more than half of it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
sentences.text: Had we taken the easy way out on GST each time, starting from 1993, we would be wringing our hands today, instead of talking about taking two hands to clap, amidst all the exciting plans under Forward Singapore.

sections.label: Worker job loss survey
sections.summary: Amid double retrenchment figures and slowing wage growth, 40% of workers saw likely job loss in three months, up from 25% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Amid double retrenchment figures and slowing wage growth, the survey revealed worrying trends, with 40% of all workers expressing the likelihood of job loss in the next three months, up from 25% in 2023.

sections.label: Lazada lay-off settlement
sections.summary: After an abrupt lay-off, Lazada Singapore and FDAWU reached an amicable settlement with an enhanced support package and training fund.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: After the abrupt lay-off, Lazada Singapore Private Limited and the Food, Drinks and Allied Workers Union (FDAWU) eventually reached an amicable settlement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The resolution includes an enhanced support package and training fund for affected members under the union's scope of representation, many of whom, in fact, are PME workers.

sections.label: NTUC representing all workers
sections.summary: With 51% of NTUC members now PMEs, NTUC will continue to represent all workers regardless of collar, age or nationality.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: With 51% of NTUC members now being PMEs, NTUC will continue to represent all workers, regardless of collars, age or nationality or, what we often say, "All can".

sections.label: AI impact on jobs
sections.summary: A World Economic Forum report says over 75% of companies plan to integrate Big Data, cloud computing and AI in five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: According to the World Economic Forum 2023's Future of Jobs report, over 75% of companies are planning to integrate Big Data, cloud computing and AI technologies in the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Based on NTUC's annual Economic Sentiments survey, 3% already experienced negative impacts on their jobs as a result of AI and 15% are worried that they will lose their jobs.

sections.label: AI and automation job displacement
sections.summary: AI and automation may displace jobs across sectors, including the 60% of Singapore's workforce who are PMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: The rise of AI and automation may lead to job displacements across sectors, including those in the high percentage of PMEs who form 60% of Singapore's workforce today.

sections.label: Union-backed CTC grant for workers
sections.summary: With union support, the company secured 70% grant approval for its CTC project, benefitting 38 workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: With support from the Singapore Manual and Mercantile Workers' Union, the company successfully secured a 70% grant approval for its CTC project, benefitting 38 workers, 12 receiving an average wage increment of 8% and 26 impacted by the implementation of a career development plan.

sections.label: e2i expanded career placement role
sections.summary: From 1 April 2024, NTUC's e2i takes over designated career centres and Jobs and Skills Centres from Workforce Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Today, I am pleased to announce that starting from 1 April 2024, NTUC's Employment and Employability Institute (e2i) will assume an expanded role in the personalised placement landscape through the transfer of designated career centres and Jobs and Skills Centres from Workforce Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: With more strategically located career and job services touch points across Singapore, NTUC's e2i will bring personalised career coaching, job matching and skills upgrading services closer to the individuals in the heartlands and help all Singaporeans across diverse work types islandwide to find better employment and employability.

sections.label: Training boost for mid-career workers
sections.summary: The speaker welcomed Budget 2024's training boost for mid-career workers above 40 and called for reviewing training funds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: I also called for the Government to review training funds and allowances to support our workers in alleviating their concern for the lack of time and finances and opportunity costs when attending training.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: So, I was particularly excited when Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced in this year's Budget a very significant training boost for mid-career workers in his Budget speech, and I thank the Government for the decisive move in Budget 2024 to recognise that our mid-career workers who are above 40 years old need more help.

sections.label: Employers supporting mid-career workers
sections.summary: The speaker hopes employers will hire, fairly pay and give training time-off to mid-career workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We look forward to more details to be announced at the Committee of Supply by the Ministries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Now that the Government has made a very significant move and NTUC has continued to step up our upskilling and job supporting efforts, I hope that the employers will join hands with us, do your part to better support our mid-career workers, to more hire more of these workers, to pay them fairly based on their skillsets and experience and to provide protected time-off for their training and consider ways to recognise their skillsets.

sections.label: SkillsFuture subsidies for workers
sections.summary: The speaker urges workers to join unions and use SkillsFuture subsidies, including $4,000 for those 40 and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: Additionally, we sincerely hope that more workers can achieve these three points: firstly, join the union to bring more security to their careers and lives; secondly, make good use of the SkillsFuture training subsidies to enhance skills and keep pace with economic transformation; and thirdly, we urge middle-aged and mid-career workers to make good use of the subsidies provided by the new SkillsFuture Level-Up programme to pursue professional courses and strengthen their employability.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: All Singaporeans aged 40 and above can receive an additional $4,000 subsidy.

sections.label: NTUC partnership and worker support
sections.summary: NTUC reaffirms partnership with Government and industry on workforce development, urges workers to join NTUC, calls for company collaboration on CTC, and thanks Government for Budget support for mid-career workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: NTUC remains committed to our partnership with the Government and the industry stakeholders with an unwavering focus on workforce development because every worker matters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mr Desmond Tan)
sentences.text: We encourage workers to join NTUC, we call on more companies to collaborate with us on CTC and extend our gratitude to Government for the substantial support for mid-career workers in this Budget.

sections.label: Retrenchments doubled in 2023
sections.summary: In 2023, retrenchments in Singapore more than doubled to 14,000, with challenges, uncertainties and volatility persisting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: In 2023, retrenchments in Singapore more than doubled to 14,000 and the myriad of challenges, uncertainties and volatility persists.

sections.label: Unemployment insurance lobbying history
sections.summary: The speaker cites Dr Goh Keng Swee's 1970 Hansard speech on unemployment insurance and ILO consultation, and notes growing MP support, Forward Singapore adoption, and DPM Lawrence Wong's Budget announcement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I have checked Hansard and found that the late Dr Goh Keng Swee, in March 1970, also in this House, spoke about and analysed the unemployment insurance, and also consulted the ILO before the Government made its stance and stated its approach.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: I am heartened that after a decade of lobbying, more MPs have joined me in this call including our Opposition MPs, that it has been adopted by the Government through Forward Singapore last October and announced by Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in his Budget Speech this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Temporary financial support for the unemployed has increasingly emerged as a key recommendation from the Labour Movement's engagements with workers and union leaders in the past few years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: It started as a key recommendation from the NTUC-SNEF PME Taskforce, which I co-chaired with SNEF in 2021 amid COVID-19, where we consulted over 10,000 members of the public, union leaders and business leaders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (Pioneer)
sentences.text: It was reiterated again in our NTUC's renewed Workers' Compact last year, following a year-long engagement with over 42,000 workers, through our #EveryWorkerMatters Conversations.

sections.label: Retrenchments expected to rise further
sections.summary: MOM's preliminary data shows retrenchments more than doubled in the past year and are expected to rise even further.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: MOM's preliminary data has shown that retrenchments have more than doubled in the past year and this is expected to rise even further.

sections.label: Income, inflation and Assurance Package
sections.summary: NTUC's survey found 63% felt income did not match cost-of-living rises, and Budget 2024 will enhance the Assurance Package by $1.9 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: In NTUC's most recent annual survey on economic sentiments, 63% of respondents felt that their income did not increase sufficiently to match the rise in the cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Many young seniors in Radin Mas have also shared with me their growing worries about retirement adequacy, wondering if their retirement nest eggs can survive being eroded by inflation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I am therefore heartened that Budget 2024 will enhance the Assurance Package by $1.9 billion.

sections.label: Social spending nearly doubled
sections.summary: Between 2010 and 2019, social spending nearly doubled to $37 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Between 2010 and 2019, we nearly doubled our social spending to $37 billion.

sections.label: PWM wage increases 2022 to 2028
sections.summary: From 2022 to 2028, workers covered by PWM can expect cumulative wage increases of up to 80%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: From 2022 to 2028, workers covered by PWM can expect cumulative wage increases of up to 80%.

sections.label: PWM expansion and ITE Progression Award
sections.summary: The Labour Movement proposed expanding PWM elements to roles like strata and pest management, and the ITE Progression Award gives ITE graduates $15,000 in top-ups for diplomas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement has proposed for elements of PWM to be expanded to more roles, such as strata management and pest management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: One of the announcements that stood out to me in this Budget was the ITE Progression Award to empower our ITE graduates to upskill to a diploma earlier in their career.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: They will get a total of $15,000 in top-ups when they complete their diploma.

sections.label: Progressive Wage Portal launch
sections.summary: MOM recently launched a Progressive Wage Portal for lower-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Most recently, MOM launched a Progressive Wage Portal for our lower-wage workers.

sections.label: JGI spending and local hires
sections.summary: From FY2020 to 2021, $6.2 billion was spent on JGI, supporting close to 709,000 local hires by 83,000 firms between September 2020 and February 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: From FY2020 to 2021, $6.2 billion was spent on JGI to boost local hires.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: It supported close to 709,000 local hires by 83,000 firms between September 2020 and February 2022.

sections.label: Budget 2024 PWCS top-up
sections.summary: In Budget 2024, the Deputy Prime Minister announced a further $1 billion top-up to PWCS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In Budget 2024, the Deputy Prime Minister announced a further $1 billion top-up to PWCS.

sections.label: Graduate employment rate drop
sections.summary: Global uncertainties have resulted in fewer jobs, and the Joint Autonomous Universities Graduate Employment Survey showed employment within six months fell to 89.6% in 2023 from 93.8% the year before.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Global uncertainties, such as shifting supply chains and geopolitical tensions, have resulted in fewer jobs being created.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: This year, the Joint Autonomous Universities Graduate Employment Survey showed that the proportion of university graduates who found employment within six months of taking their final exams dropped to 89.6% in 2023 from 93.8% the year before.

sections.label: Subsidies for second diploma
sections.summary: The speaker welcomed Budget 2024 subsidies for middle-aged Singaporeans to pursue a second diploma and the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Over the past three Budgets, I have called on the Government to provide subsidies for Singaporeans to pursue a second degree or diploma to remain future-ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I am heartened with the Government's move in Budget 2024 to enable Singaporeans middle-aged and above to receive full Government subsidies to pursue a second diploma.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: There is also the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, with a SkillsFuture credit of $4,000 and monthly training allowance of up to $3,000.

sections.label: SkillsFuture age and AI support
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Government lowers the SkillsFuture Credit eligibility age from 25 and provides subsidised diplomas for those affected by AI and green transition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Furthermore, for those affected or displaced by AI or the green transition, they would arguably need the same support as those in their middle-age.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I hope that the Government can consider lowering the SkillsFuture Credit eligibility age down from the current 25 years old to empower more younger people to upskill and reskill, and to provide subsidised diplomas for those affected by AI and green transition.

sections.label: Local shareholding and young workers
sections.summary: The speaker suggests removing the 30% local shareholding condition and says NTUC will support young workers, citing a conversation with 42,000 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Perhaps there is scope to remove the 30% local shareholding condition to expand the reach of such programmes to our MNCs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In this new chapter, we need to help our young workers to put on the full armour of adaptability and resilience in a world whereby they may be assailed on all fronts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: We need to help our young workers understand the new economy's impact on their livelihoods and strengthen their career paths.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: NTUC will remain alongside each and every worker through the uncertain times because #EveryWorkerMatters.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In this respect, the NTUC concluded a year-long conversation with our workers, 42,000 workers to be precise, to understand the dreams and challenges of our workers in modern day Singapore.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements survey
sections.summary: An NTUC and PAP Women's Wing survey of about 3,000 working caregivers found close to 90% said FWAs were important to stay or return to work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: In a recent NTUC Women and Family-PAP Women’s Wing survey of some 3,000 working caregivers, close to 90% said that FWAs would be a very important factor for them to choose to stay or return to the workplace.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: With over 12,000 companies being signatories to the 2017 Tripartite Standards for Flexible Work Arrangements, and the tailwinds afforded by COVID-19, the time is now to make FWAs a workplace norm.

sections.label: Women returners training programme
sections.summary: A paid pre-employment training programme with flexi-time and flexi-place arrangements has attracted some 800 women returners into its pipeline.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Using a mix of a paid pre-employment training programme, with flexi-time and flexi-place work arrangements, the programme has since attracted some 800 women returners into its prospective pipeline.

sections.label: Riders working seven days
sections.summary: Riders said platform incentive structures directly affect their livelihoods, leading many to work seven days a week.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Our riders shared with me that due to the way that some platforms structure their incentives, which directly affects their livelihoods, many riders end up having to work seven days in a week.

sections.label: Platform withheld delivery worker vouchers
sections.summary: A platform refused to give a worker $250 in vouchers he earned, despite appeals and his poor medical condition.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: He had missed a message from the platform, relaying that they had moved earlier the last date of collection for the vouchers that he had rightfully earned as part of his incentives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: It was $250 in vouchers and, even with several appeals and appeals from the Delivery Association and explanations of his poor medical condition, the platform refused to budge on their decision to not give him the vouchers.

sections.label: Platform workers injury retirement safety nets
sections.summary: The Advisory Committee on Platform Workers recommended workplace injury and retirement safety nets for vulnerable workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The Advisory Committee on Platform Workers has recommended the need to set workplace injury and retirement safety nets for our workers, many who are vulnerable, like Mr K.

sections.label: Supporting skilled trades and crafts
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to partner with guilds and unions to make skilled trades a career choice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We have seen some good, early successes of attracting younger plumbers into the trade, many who have gone on to become their own bosses in the plumbing world.

sentences.speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: I call on the Government to support our skilled trades and crafts by partnering with our guilds and unions in making skilled trades an exciting career choice once again, for our youths and mid-careerists.

sections.label: Freelancers recovering money from micro-firm
sections.summary: VICPA has helped freelance creative and media professionals recover a six-figure sum from Company A, which faced two contractor terms.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: From late-2023, NTUC's Visual, Audio, Creative Content Professionals Association (VICPA) that I serve, has been helping a group of freelance creative and media professionals to recover a six-figure sum in total from a production micro-firm, Company A.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: What was concerning were two terms imposed by a main contractor on Company A: one, Company A was to finance the project from the outset at a tune of $30,000 to $50,000 per project; and two, Company A could only collect all payment after project completion, and this could be three to six months later.

sections.label: Main contractors adopted Tripartite Standards
sections.summary: In both cases, the main contractors were adopters of Tripartite Standards on contracting freelancers.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In both cases, the main contractors in question were adopters of the Tripartite Standards relevant to contracting and/or procuring services from freelancers.

sections.label: Validating Tripartite Standards for freelancers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Government could level up and validate Tripartite Standards guiding fair contracting with freelancers and micro-firms.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As firms continue their march to de-risk, could the Government consider levelling up and validating the Tripartite Standards that guide businesses to be fair and ethical, when contracting with freelancers and micro-firms?

sections.label: Freelancer power imbalance, stagnated rates
sections.summary: Many freelancers face power imbalance with service buyers and stagnated rates.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Second, many freelancers are subject to power imbalance with service buyers and face stagnated rates.

sections.label: Buyer-dictated rates erode freelancer earnings
sections.summary: Power imbalance forces freelancers to accept buyer-dictated rates and terms, eroding hourly rates in creative, media and coaching sectors.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Despite the feelings of inequity, the power imbalance between buyer and freelancer means that freelancers have little choice but to oblige with buyer-dictated rates and terms.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These trends have led to eroding hourly rates for many freelancers in the creative, media and coaching sectors, including those contracted directly or through sub-contractors for Government-commissioned work.

sections.label: MOM update self-employed support recommendations
sections.summary: The proposal asks MOM to update the 2018 Tripartite Workgroup's recommendations on support for self-employed persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It would also provide the relevant Government bodies useful insights to update budgets for fair and equitable procurement of services from these freelancers and micro-firms.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, to build sustainable and viable freelancing livelihoods and careers, I propose that MOM update the 2018 Tripartite Workgroup's recommendations on support for self-employed persons.

sections.label: Technology transforming jobs estimate
sections.summary: The World Economic Forum estimated 1.1 billion jobs could be radically transformed by technology this decade.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The World Economic Forum estimated that 1.1 billion jobs could be radically transformed by technology in this decade.

sections.label: Levelling up Tripartite Standards
sections.summary: This proposes levelling up and validating Tripartite Standards guiding businesses contracting with freelancers and micro-firms.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, levelling up and validating the Tripartite Standards that guide businesses to be fair and ethical when contracting with freelancers and micro-firms.

sections.label: Refresh workgroup recommendations, caregiving grants
sections.summary: This proposes refreshing the 2018 Tripartite Workgroup's recommendations and having caregiving grants go beyond defraying caregiving expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Third, relook at and refresh the 2018 Tripartite Workgroup’s Recommendations on support for self-employed persons.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Fourth, have caregiving grants go beyond defraying caregiving expenses.

sections.label: Freelancers share of resident workers
sections.summary: Freelancers make up close to one in 10 of Singapore's resident workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms See Jinli Jean (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Freelancers make up close to one in 10 of Singapore's resident workers.

sections.label: WIS eligibility for lower-wage workers
sections.summary: Lower-wage workers earning $3,000 or less will be eligible for WIS in January 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Last week, the Government also announced that lower-wage workers who earn $3,000 or less will be eligible for WIS in January 2025.

sections.label: Call to ringfence lower-wage workers
sections.summary: The speaker calls on the Government to consider ringfencing lower-wage workers from problems of resetting benefits during contractual changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Advocating force for change is essential to ensure a fair and supportive work environment fostering stability and acknowledging the contributions of all workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Therefore, I call on the Government to consider ringfencing lower-wage workers to protect them from associated problems stemming from the practice of resetting benefits during contractual changes.

sections.label: PWCS enhancements welcomed
sections.summary: The Labour Movement appreciates PWCS enhancements raising the co-funding wage ceiling to $3,000 and enhancing co-funding levels for 2024 wage increases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement appreciates the Government's enhancements to the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS), including raising the wage ceiling for co-funding from $2,500 to $3,000 in qualifying years 2025 and 2026, and enhancing co-funding levels for wage increases given in 2024.

sections.label: LQS raised to $1,600
sections.summary: The Labour Movement welcomes the Government's move to raise the LQS to $1,600 in July this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Labour Movement welcomes the Government's move to raise the LQS to $1,600 in July this year, up from $1,400 previously.

sections.label: Engaging Malay/Muslim workers
sections.summary: NTUC with WSG and MENDAKI engaged over 5,000 Malay/Muslim workers, and MENDAKI referred over 140 W@W participants to e2i.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: NTUC, with WSG and MENDAKI, through career fairs and the recent Jobs and Skills Carnival, more than 5,000 Malay/Muslim workers were engaged and close to 20% them had received further coaching and guidance through Focus Area 4’s initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: MENDAKI has referred over 140 participants from Women At Work (W@W) to NTUC’s e2i for job assistance from January to December 2023.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Mid-Career Support
sections.summary: A $4,000 top-up in May 2024, Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy, and monthly allowance of up to $3,000 for up to 24 months for selected full-time courses under the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: A top up of $4,000 in May 2024 and the Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy is a boost for individual to continue upskill and seek better employability outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In addition, the monthly allowance of up to $3,000, up to 24 months, for selected full-time courses under the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance will be welcomed by many.

sections.label: Older Workers in Workforce
sections.summary: Workers aged 55 and above make up more than a quarter of Singapore's resident workforce today.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Workers aged 55 and above make up more than a quarter of our resident workforce today.

sections.label: Retirement and Re-employment Ages
sections.summary: Most older workers surveyed wanted to continue working, and the speaker calls for the next increase in retirement and re-employment ages by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Out of the 10 who were there, eight and a half of them would say that they wanted to continue working and, out of these eight and a half, or 85% of the older workers who participated in our conversations, six out of the eight and a half, hoped to continue working in their current jobs or in the current industry where they have accumulated experience and value.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And just to remind fellow Members here, these 2030 goals of statutory retirement age of 65 and statutory re-employment age ceiling of 70 was the work of the Tripartite Workgroup (Older Workers), whose report came out in 2019, and the roadmap was endorsed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: I, therefore, call on the Government to announce the next step increase in the retirement and re-employment ages soonest and to give reasonable notice to both business and workers, so that both sides can get ready in good time.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: We should act promptly because we are already practically halfway there in terms of timeframe so that we can implement the next increase by, say, in two years' time, that is, by 2026.

sections.label: Company Training Committees Funding
sections.summary: Active CTCs help businesses transform and workers train in relevant skills, with $100 million funding to NTUC to scale up CTCs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: Through active CTCs, businesses can transform faster and workers of all ages can be helped to be trained in relevant skills and to be able to grow with the companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: And, here, I again thank the Government for the $100 million funding to NTUC to scale-up CTCs in order to achieve real outcomes for all stakeholders.

sections.label: Workplace Fairness Legislation
sections.summary: The Workplace Fairness legislation and Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements Requests will build on existing tripartite mechanisms against workplace discrimination, including age bias.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: For this reason, I look forward to the Workplace Fairness legislation and the Tripartite Guidelines on Flexible Work Arrangements Requests that the Government will be introducing.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: The Workplace Fairness legislation will build on existing tripartite mechanisms, such as the Tripartite Alliance for Fair and Progressive Employment Practices (TAFEP), the Tripartite Alliance for Dispute Management (TADM) and relevant joint guidelines to give even greater confidence or fair play to workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Mr Heng Chee How)
sentences.text: This will be a strong national signal against various forms of workplace discrimination, including age bias.

sections.label: Employment Support Measures
sections.summary: Budget 2023 announced the Uplifting Employment Credit for ex-offenders, enhanced Comlink+ packages were announced, and Budget 2024 reaffirmed re-employment support for involuntary unemployment with increased reskilling support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In Budget 2023 itself, Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence Wong announced the Uplifting Employment Credit for employers to hire ex-offenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Late last year, the Government announced the enhanced Comlink+ packages, which involved matching repayment to creditors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And in Budget 2024, while we yet await the details, the Deputy Prime Minister reaffirmed the intention first announced by Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong to move forward with re-employment support to those in involuntary unemployment, alongside significant increases to reskilling support and training allowances.

sections.label: GDP growth and productivity focus
sections.summary: The Government aims for 2% to 3% average annual GDP growth over the next decade, focusing on productivity and innovation within labour, land and carbon constraints.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Government aims to achieve an average of 2% to 3% GDP growth per annum over the next decade, with a focus on productivity and innovation, while recognising the constraints of labour, land and carbon.

sections.label: Budget 2024 AI investment
sections.summary: Budget 2024 sets out an investment of more than $1 billion over five years into AI compute, including advanced chips, talent and industry development.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: To support the National AI Strategy and to further catalyse AI activities, Budget 2024 sets out an investment of more than $1 billion over the next five years into AI compute, including, notably, in advanced chips, talent and industry development.

sections.label: 10-20-70 rule for scaling AI
sections.summary: A practitioner's 10-20-70 rule states scaling AI is 10% algorithms, 20% tech foundations, and 70% people, processes and change management.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: But if I may offer a practitioner's perspective, scaling AI requires a holistic effort.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: We call it the 10-20-70 rule: 10% of the effort is in the algorithms, the generative AI, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML) models; 20% in the tech and IT foundations, the model infrastructure and machine learning operations (MLOps), data quality and availability, importantly, architecture design, app integration, cloud migration and other tools; but 70% is about people and processes, ways of working, business process reinvention, adoption at scale, organisation and talent strategy and change management.

sections.label: Deploying AI use cases at scale
sections.summary: Value comes from deploying horizontal and vertical use cases at scale, with potential in high-impact cases in sectors like financial services or transport and logistics.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While the technology is important, the value only comes from deploying use cases at scale based on a thorough assessment of value and ease of deployment, both horizontal use cases like customer service, that can be adopted across industries, as well as vertical use cases in specific industries, like drug discovery in healthcare.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is significant potential to tackle a few, high impact use cases that reimagine how things are done, not only in an individual company but an entire sector, particularly in sectors where we are already advantaged, say, financial services or transport and logistics, to optimise at a system level and create new sources of differentiation and competitive advantage for Singapore in these sectors.

sections.label: Strong centre for AI strategy
sections.summary: The speaker suggests making AI and the National AI Strategy a priority of the Prime Minister, supported by a central team, with parallels to SNDGO.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While Ministries and agencies have the domain expertise and should drive the AI work in their respective sectors, there is a case to be made for having a strong centre that adds value by prioritising investments with the greatest public return, providing transparency and accountability, setting a coherent long-term strategy, challenging the Ministries and agencies on their AI priorities, removing barriers and resolving conflicts with other areas of the Government and drawing on best practices from across the Government and the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, I suggest that the AI and the National AI Strategy be made a priority of the Prime Minister, supported by a central team, with some parallels to the Smart Nation and Digital Government Office (SNDGO).

sections.label: Strong centre for coordinated AI response
sections.summary: Cross-cutting issues strain a lead Ministry model while joint ownership could be fragmented, so a strong centre is needed for fast coordinated response.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The complexities and cross-cutting issues involved will put a big strain on a model of Government based on a lead Ministry or lead agency, while a joint ownership model could be too fragmented.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: A strong centre is, therefore, needed to ensure fast and coordinated analysis, assessment and response that the public expects.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: AI has to be a part of a bold but credible growth plan.

sections.label: Budget 2024 GDP growth target
sections.summary: Budget 2024 plans a long-run GDP growth target of 2% to 3% for Singapore's mature economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Budget 2024 plans for a long-run GDP target growth of 2% to 3%, given Singapore's mature economy.

sections.label: FY2023 revenue and GST collections
sections.summary: FY2023 revenue beat expectations but GST collections were $1 billion lower; FY2024 top-up is $20.4 billion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While Government revenue in FY2023 was overall better than expected, I note that GST collections were $1 billion lower than estimated due to weaker imports.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The expected top-up of funds is $20.4 billion in FY2024.

sections.label: Business cost pressures and Budget support
sections.summary: Business owners face cost-of-survival pressures, so the Budget offers a 50% corporate income tax rebate and $2,000 payouts for non-profitable firms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Some business owners say that they face "cost of survival" pressures, in tandem with the high cost-of-living pressures faced by individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I, therefore, welcome the Budget's support measures that bolster near-term resilience, such as the 50% corporate income tax rebate as well as the newly introduced and generous $2,000 cash payout for non-profitable firms with at least one employee under the Enterprise Support Package.

sections.label: MHA anti-scam efforts and losses
sections.summary: MHA's anti-scam measures kept losses flat at $650 million, but scam cases rose 46% to 46,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: From the Anti-Scam Command to the ScamShield app and the Online Criminal Harms Act, the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has been relentless in its fight against the scourge of scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This has helped to keep losses flat at $650 million last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, the amount is still significant, and cases have soared by 46% to an unprecedented 46,000 cases!

sections.label: Youth drug abuse new abusers
sections.summary: CNB reported more than half of new abusers arrested last year were below age 30.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: The trend of drug abuse by youths is therefore worrying, as the Central Narcotics Bureau (CNB) reported more than half of new abusers arrested last year were below the age of 30.

sections.label: Neighbourhood noise complaint levels
sections.summary: Monthly noise complaints averaged over 2,000 in the last year, more than five times pre-pandemic levels.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Regrettably, the issue of noise has continued to cause friction in our neighbourhoods, with monthly complaints in the last year averaging over 2,000 cases, more than five times higher than pre-pandemic levels.

sections.label: Budget 2024 and Forward SG
sections.summary: Budget 2024 is principled, disciplined and pragmatic, and a first instalment to realise Forward SG goals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Singapore, like other countries, faces similar pressures like cost of living, on top of more unique challenges as a small island-state dependent on an open economy amid a trying global environment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Thanks to good governance and financial strength accumulated from our Reserves and its prudent use along with the diligence of those who came before us.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I am glad that Budget 2024 did not succumb to populist and unsustainable initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Budget 2024 is underpinned by fundamentals that is principled, disciplined and pragmatic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Derrick Goh (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Budget 2024 has been a fitting first instalment to realise the Forward SG goals.

sections.label: Retrenchments and unemployment in 2023
sections.summary: Retrenchments in 2023 rose to 14,320 while unemployment stayed at 2.7%, with most retrenched workers re-entering within six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: According to the advanced labour estimates released by MOM on 31 January 2024, the number of retrenchments in 2023 spiked to 14,320, more than double the record low of 6,440 in 2022.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Notwithstanding this, the unemployment rate remained at a relatively low rate of 2.7% in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The MOM report also indicated that this was partly due to "global economic headwinds on outward-oriented sectors such as wholesale trade, IT services and electronics." However, statistics also showed that most retrenched workers re-enter the workforce within six months.

sections.label: Support for the unemployed
sections.summary: The speaker supports the proposal for greater support for the unemployed amid more job market challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Against this backdrop of even more challenges coming into the job market, I support the proposal for greater support for the unemployed.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit top-up and allowance
sections.summary: This provides a $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top-up and an allowance of up to $3,000 a month for full-time courses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This, to me, seems to be an alternative but which could work quite well together with the unemployment support scheme.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This provides a $4,000 top-up to the SkillsFuture Credit a person has and provides an allowance of up to $3,000 a month while a person is attending full-time courses.

sections.label: ITE Progression Award
sections.summary: The ITE Progression Award gives $15,000 to encourage ITE graduates to pursue diploma qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Along the theme of investing in our people, the ITE Progression Award also gives encouragement to our ITE graduates to pursue diploma qualification.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This is an aspiration for many ITE graduates and the support of $15,000 will be helpful, particularly to those from lower-income families.

sections.label: WIS and Progressive Wage Credit Scheme
sections.summary: WIS and the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme will now cover workers with incomes of up to $3,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: WIS will now cover workers with incomes of up to $3,000 while the Progressive Wage Credit Scheme will also cover employees with an income of up to $3,000.

sections.label: SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme grant
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister introduced the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, providing a $4,000 grant and a training allowance of up to $3,000 a month.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In this Budget, the Deputy Prime Minister has introduced the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme, which provides a $4,000 grant as well as a training allowance of up to $3,000 a month.

sections.label: SkillsFuture support for upskilling
sections.summary: The $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit top-up, extended Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy and new Mid-Career Training Allowance show the Government's dedication to aiding all Singaporeans in upskilling, including PwDs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Initiatives like the $4,000 top-up in SkillsFuture Credit, the extension of the Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy and the introduction of the SkillsFuture Mid-Career Training Allowance highlight the Government's dedication to aiding all Singaporeans in upskilling, including PwDs.

sections.label: Course fee funding for PWDs
sections.summary: Job-seeking PWDs registered with SG Enable receive additional course fee funding support of up to 95%.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Job-seeking PWDs registered with SG Enable receive additional course fee funding support of up to 95%.

sections.label: Australia accommodations versus Singapore
sections.summary: Australia legally requires approved training organisations to provide reasonable accommodations for PwDs, but Singapore does not, despite ratifying the CRPD in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: In Australia, where Singapore's Skills Qualification Framework is modeled after, their approved training organisations (ATOs) are legally required to provide reasonable accommodations for PwDs in teaching, learning and assessment.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, this is not a requirement in Singapore, despite having ratified the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) in 2013.

sections.label: Few training providers offer accommodations
sections.summary: Based on SG Enable's Annual Reports from 2017 to 2020, only an average of 24 out of close to 1,000 training providers do so each year.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Based on the SG Enable’s Annual Reports from 2017 to 2020, only an average of 24 out of close to 1,000 training providers do so each year.

sections.label: Proposal for inclusive training providers
sections.summary: The speaker proposes MOE require relevant training providers, especially those running Mid-Career Training Allowance courses, to work with the Enabling Academy on reasonable accommodations for PwDs.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: But the launch of the Level-Up Programme presents an immediate opportunity to integrate inclusivity into our CET sector.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: I propose for MOE’s consideration to require the relevant training providers, particularly those running courses that qualify for the Mid-Career Training Allowance, to work with the Enabling Academy on assessing reasonable accommodations for PwDs and where found reasonable, to make provisions.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Once more, I must applaud the Enabling Academy for your outstanding accomplishment in achieving and offering more than 700 disability-friendly courses within a brief time period.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: However, we aim to ensure that PwDs who possess the capability to do so are able to access the 29,000 courses available on the main SkillsFuture portal, provided that necessary accommodations are put in place.

sections.label: MAS guidelines for disabled customers
sections.summary: MAS is preparing guidelines for financial institutions on fair practices towards customers, requiring clear directives on rejection, loading and exclusion criteria for individuals with disabilities, autism and mental health disorders.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: As MAS prepares to introduce guidelines for financial institutions to embrace fair and responsible practices towards customers in mid-2024, it is imperative that clear directives are established on how rejection, loading and exclusion criteria should be set for individuals with disabilities, autism and mental health disorders.

sections.label: Third-party panel for insurance disputes
sections.summary: An objective panel of third-party evaluators comprising Government officials, industry representatives, medical professionals and disability experts is proposed to resolve disputes and foster a more equitable insurance environment.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: To ensure a more impartial process, it is vital to institute an objective panel of third-party evaluators comprising of Government officials, industry representatives, medical professionals and disability experts to resolve disputes and foster a more equitable insurance environment.

sections.label: Royalty income tax concession withdrawal
sections.summary: The Budget stated the 10% tax concession on gross royalties for authors, composers and choreographers will be withdrawn in phases from YA2027, with no concession from YA2029, and taxpayers taxed on net royalties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In this year's Budget, it was stated that in order to ensure parity in the treatment of royalty income, the current tax concession of taxing only 10% of gross royalties earned by authors, composers and choreographers or any company wholly owned by them will be withdrawn in phases, with effect from Year of Assessment (YA) 2027.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For YA2027 and YA2028, eligible taxpayers may continue to claim the tax concession based on higher specified rates but with effect from YA2029, the concession will no longer be available.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Taxpayers will be required to report the net amount of royalties earned and will be taxed on them accordingly.

sections.label: Renovation tax deduction and artwork purchases
sections.summary: Enhancements to the section 14N tax deduction for renovation or refurbishment expenditure are noted, but deductions remain disallowed for antiques and fine art, with capital allowance for artworks clarified only for hospitality-related businesses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The next change I would like to address concerns the enhancements to the tax deduction for Renovation or Refurbishment expenditure, under section 14N of the Income Tax Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This, to my mind, is important acknowledgment of the work of designers in renovation and refurbishment works, and offers a good incentive for businesses that pay their designers a fair and equitable wage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: That being said, deductions are still expressly disallowed on the purchases of antiques and any type of fine art, including painting, drawing, print, calligraphy, mosaic, sculpture, pottery or art installations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: While general capital allowance deductions may be available for the purchase of artworks that qualify as "plant", the Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore (IRAS) has only clarified so far that qualifying conditions may be met in hospitality-related businesses, for example in clubs, restaurants and hotels.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Artwork purchases in other types of settings, such as in offices, may not qualify.

sections.label: Review of section 14N conditions
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes the enhancements to tax deductions under section 14N and hopes the Government will re-evaluate the scheme's conditions to encourage art purchases in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To conclude on this point, while I welcome the enhancements to the tax deductions available under section 14N, I hope the Government will continue to re-evaluate the conditions of the scheme in future and consider whether these conditions can be adjusted to encourage purchases of art in Singapore.

sections.label: Larger families and multilateralism
sections.summary: Larger families, especially those with seniors and children, get more help, and competition and confrontation of multilateralism can be damaging for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Larger families – especially those with seniors and children – get more help.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: This competition and confrontation of multilateralism can be damaging for us in Singapore.

sections.label: Ageing population and vouchers
sections.summary: It states Singapore has a shrinking and rapidly ageing population, and that vouchers or rebates cannot sustainably lift living standards long term.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Beyond a shrinking population, we are also a rapidly ageing one and no amount of vouchers or rebates will ever be a sustainable way of lifting the standards of our people over a long period of time.

sections.label: Upskilling greying workforce commitment
sections.summary: It states the author is heartened by Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence's commitment to focus efforts on upskilling the greying workforce.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For this reason, I am heartened by Deputy Prime Minister Lawrence's commitment to focus efforts on the objective of upskilling our greying workforce.

sections.label: Unused credits across ages
sections.summary: It states an article noted that across all ages, seven in 10 people have not used the credits since 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The article noted that across all ages, seven in 10 people have not used the credits since it started in 2015.

sections.label: Training barriers for workers
sections.summary: It cites reports that 77% lacked time for training, 55% lacked employer support, and calls for tackling system barriers like inflexible working hours.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: According to the recent National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) Every Worker Matters Report, 77% of respondents felt they lacked the time to attend training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A separate 2021 study shared that this could be due to fatigue from work and other life commitments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We say "活到老, 学到老", but in order to effectively put this into practice we must also tackle system barriers, such as inflexible working hours – 55% of workers felt they lacked the support from their employers from self-initiated training.

sections.label: MNC headquarters in Singapore
sections.summary: It states that as of 2023, 4,200 MNC headquarters are here and Singapore is a gateway to Asia, but that trend is being challenged.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: As of 2023, it is reported that the headquarters of 4,200 MNCs can be found here and is the base of choice for companies as a gateway to Asia, but we are starting to see signs of that trend being challenged.

sections.label: Businesses ready to relocate
sections.summary: It cites a 2023 European Chamber of Commerce survey finding 7 in 10 businesses ready to relocate employees without relief from rising costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: A 2023 survey by the European Chamber of Commerce found that "7 in 10 businesses indicated that they are ready to relocate their employees outside of Singapore if there are no relief from rising operating costs." When businesses leave, jobs leave too.

sections.label: Social isolation and dementia risk
sections.summary: Studies suggest social isolation was linked to around 50% higher dementia risk, prompting calls for elderly mental well-being focus and reference to the UK's loneliness commission.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Recent studies suggest that social isolation was associated with around a 50% increased risk of dementia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I reiterate my calls for there to be targeted focus on mental well-being for our elderly and perhaps we can even take reference from the United Kingdom's Commission on Loneliness, where a Minister for Loneliness was appointed and there was strong cross-sector collaboration to tackle this issue.

sections.label: Stronger culture of giving
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister announced measures to build a stronger giving culture, including the Charities Capability Fund Collaboration Grant and philanthropy efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: To this end, I am glad that the Deputy Prime Minister also announced measures to further build a stronger culture of giving that encourages collaboration – for example, the Charities Capability Fund Collaboration Grant and the efforts to work with philanthropy on the needs in society.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We must work with philanthropic foundations, individuals and corporates to be strategic, complementary and catalytic in how we deploy capital towards social needs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I hope that the recently established SG Government Partnerships Office can play a role to involve ideas and efforts from our citizens, coordinate efforts and efficiently scale successful projects beyond pilots.

sections.label: Budget for everyone
sections.summary: This Budget shows Singapore is a city for everyone, offering something for everyone with immediate relief and long-term policies.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Budget makes it clear that Singapore is a city for everyone and that Singapore's future belongs to everyone.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This Budget has something for everyone and provides both immediate relief for individuals and organisations, as well as practical and affordable policies and programmes for long-term growth and sustainability.

sections.label: Targeted support for low-income families
sections.summary: Initiatives are available to all families but targeted towards low-income or financially stressed families, delivering greatest benefit to those with greatest need.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These initiatives are available to all families, yet, as is appropriate, are also targeted towards those families on low incomes or living with significant financial stress.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I welcome this targeted approach, as it is important that such initiatives deliver the greatest benefit to those with the greatest need.

sections.label: Targeted personal support for families
sections.summary: Besides financial assistance, targeted personal support is needed, including financial planning, parenting, life-skills, employment, housing, and mental health support.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As well as providing financial assistance to families in need, we also need to offer targeted personal support, including financial planning, parenting programmes, life-skills, employment and housing support and mental health and well-being support.

sections.label: Lifelong learning for all Singaporeans
sections.summary: Lifelong learning benefits society regardless of economic benefit and is relevant to all Singaporeans, including the unemployed and platform, low-wage or manual workers.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Lifelong learning is positive in and of itself and benefits society as whole, regardless of whether the learning leads to immediate or identifiable organisation or economic benefits.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is also important to recognise that lifelong learning is relevant to all Singaporeans, including the unemployed and those in platform, low-wage or manual employment.

sections.label: Singapore retirement income rankings and planning
sections.summary: Singapore's retirement income system ranked 7th internationally, but OCBC reported only two in 10 Singaporeans on track in 2023, and a 2022 survey found seven in 10 elderly Singaporeans received regular family cash allowances.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In a recent report by Mercer, Singapore's retirement income system ranked 7th internationally, only falling behind Nordic and Northern European countries and Australia.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Despite this, in 2023, OCBC reported that only two in 10 Singaporeans are on track when it comes to retirement planning.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: And in 2022, the Retirement and Health Survey reported that seven in 10 elderly Singaporeans received regular cash allowance from their family.
